#2847. Tre’Davious White to the rescue? Bills’ battered secondary may need a familiar face

There were a couple of surprises on the Buffalo Bills' first injury report of Week 11, with the team beginning practice on Wednesday for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.

None of the starting offensive linemen were sidelined today. Well, that's not entirely accurate — right guard O'Cyrus Torrence, the only lineman not dealing with an injury last week, was on Wednesday's report, but for personal reasons rather than an injury.

But the rest of the surprises on today's report? They weren't of the fun variety.

None of these are particularly surprising. Maybe Kincaid. The Bills' top tight end seems to be playing some version of "Spin the Wheel" when it comes to injuries this season. Weeks 8 and 9, it was a chest injury. Last week, it was an ankle. Now he's keeping the ankle ailment and adding a thumb injury to go with it for Week 11.

Otherwise, these injuries were evident during Sunday's game, so it's no surprise that any of the players listed here are getting another day — or three — off.

Here, we have the group that decided to surprise this week. None of them were on last week's injury list, so the injuries all came during or after Sunday's game at MetLife Stadium. That turf is unforgiving, but not all of these may have happened on game day.

We did see Hooker coming out of the medical tent Sunday, but never got any confirmation from the Bills as to why. Now we know it had something to do with his knee.

We saw Bishop getting attention from trainers on the sideline. He was seen wincing as they manipulated his arm.

It's Hamlin that gives us reason to pause. It's not great that the Bills have three injured safeties. Plus Hamlin has spent significant snaps replacing Alford, who's dealing with a concussion right now, at nickel.

Sal Capaccio with WGR550 reported seeing Hamlin in a boot and using a scooter at the end of practice. That, information — along with a limited designation — would indicate Hamlin started practice healthy. An in-practice injury that puts him in an immobilizer is not a good sign that Hamlin will play on Sunday.

The big news here is Shavers. Head coach Joe Brady announced before practice that the team was moving Shavers to the active roster. Shavers started the season on PUP after tearing his ACL in playoff action against the Jacksonville Jaguars this past January.

The Bills thought they solved their defensive back problem. They cut C.J. Gardner-Johnson, signed Amani Hooker, got Dee Alford back from an injury, discovered versatility in Damar Hamlin, and found that rookie Davison Igbinosun was doing well at boundary corner.

Now they're suddenly facing a shortage once again. Hamlin and Christian Benford aren't a lock to play Sunday. Alford has to work through the league's concussion protocol. And, if they do play, Bishop and Hooker may not be full speed.

The current uninjured Buffalo secondary would look like Jordan Hancock at NCB, Sam Franklin, Jr. and Jalon Kilgore at safety; Maxwell Hairston and Igbinosun on the boundaries.

The answer may just be a veteran. Today, Brady said that Tre'Davious White was brought in to help this team win. On Monday, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said that he feels White is ready to step up if needed.

The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday announced pricing, effective January 1, 2027, for payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, such as the clearing of checks, automated clearing house (ACH) transactions, instant payments, and wholesale payment and settlement services.

By law, the Federal Reserve must establish fees to recover the costs, including imputed costs, of providing payment services over the long run. The Federal Reserve expects to recover 101.5 percent of actual and imputed expenses in 2027, including the return on equity that would have been earned if a private-sector firm provided the services. Overall, price changes for 2027 will result in an estimated 1.4 percent average price increase for established, mature services.

In addition, the Federal Reserve Banks announced changes to streamline and adjust their check services. As described in the request for information on check services issued last year, the volume of checks processed by the Federal Reserve Banks is declining, but checks remain an important payment instrument for many consumers and businesses. The changes were informed by public feedback and ensure that the Federal Reserve Banks continue to provide check services efficiently. The adjustments include optimizing check processing windows during low-volume periods, increasing fees that banks and credit unions pay to process checks, and other operational updates. These changes do not impact consumers' and businesses' ability to pay with or receive checks and only impact how banks and credit unions process checks with Federal Reserve Banks.

The entire 2027 fee schedule for all of the Federal Reserve's payment services is published on FRBservices.org®. Additional information on the Federal Reserve's payments services, including service usage statistics, is available on the Board's website.

The Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Reserve Board, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency today announced that they will extend, until December 16, the comment period for proposed guidance on managing risks associated with third-party relationships. Comments on the proposal were originally due November 16.

The proposed guidance reflects the agencies' supervisory experience and lessons learned from examining financial institutions' third-party risk management practices. It is intended to help banks and credit unions tailor their risk management practices to the risks associated with individual third-party relationships. The proposed guidance takes a principles-based approach and, like all supervisory guidance, is non-binding.

When finalized, the federal bank regulatory agencies plan to rescind existing third-party risk management guidance and replace it with the finalized guidance to promote consistency and prudent innovation in the banking industry. NCUA also plans to rescind its existing third-party risk management guidance and will conduct its own reviews to update related guidance as needed.

Also today, the Federal Reserve Board separately announced that it will extend, until December 16, the comment period on a proposed third-party risk management guide specifically for Federal Reserve-supervised traditional community banks.

#2837. Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

The five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

#2829. Game Preview #16: Wolves vs Knicks Game Thread

Following Thursday's drunken back-and-forth beautiful mess of a come-from-behind win, it's time for Karl-Anthony Towns and the NBA Champion New York Knicks to come to town for their first matchup of the season. Despite winning seven of their last eight games, this will be the Wolves' third game in four nights after having a very physical back-to-back against the Portland Trail Blazers.

Meanwhile, the Knicks have won six of their last eight games and will now travel to Minnesota at the vert tail end of a four-game road trip. They most recently played Tuesday night in Toronto where they took care of a Kawhi Leonard-less Raptors team in the clutch.

It is Karl-Anthony Towns that deserves first billing in this matchup. In his previous two visits to Target Center since the trade, KAT is averaging 36 points, 16.5 rebounds, 3.5 assists, and is a +37 in all his minutes in the opposing team's uniform in Minneapolis.

At an 8-6 overall record, don't let the Knicks middling record fool you into thinking this team is just cruising through the regular season with a championship hangover. Since their 0-3 start, the Knicks are 8-3 with all of their losses in that time coming within single digits. In those 11 games, they are the third ranked team in net rating, trailing just the San Antonio Spurs and Boston Celtics. They are traveling to Minneapolis with a fully healthy squad and will be looking to stack more wins to climb out of the mire of the middle of the Eastern Conference.

Who: Minnesota Timberwolves (11-4) vs New York Knicks (8-6)

Where: Target Center, Minneapolis Minnesota

Key Strength Stat: Points in the paint (5th)

Key Weakness Stat: Assist Percentage (28th)

Spider-Man Pointing Meme Stat: Second Chance Points (3rd)

Key Strength Stat: Offensive Rebounding Percentage (1st)

Spider-Man Pointing Meme Stat: Second Chance Points (1st)

Over the last ten games, the Wolves are second in the league in points in the paint thanks in large part to Ayo Dosunmo's increased usage and desire to win a footrace to the rim each time he catches the ball. The Knicks are the third best team at defending the paint thanks to a core of very versatile wing defenders who are able to switch on everything and stay in prime position defensively. Couple their paint defense with being the best rebounding team in the league and it is clear where their money is made on the defensive end.

They want to force you to hit shots from midrange and beyond, and then grab rebounds with their long and athletic wings.

The Wolves are no slouches themselves with the sixth best rebounding percentage. They utilize a very similar front court when they are fully healthy. The Knicks play at the slowest pace in the league and utilize a half-court offense that is going to feature a lot of Jalen Brunson trying to get to the rim and draw (or at least make it look like he's drawn) contact. The Wolves defend well without fouling (5th best opponent free throw rate), but the NBA Finals MVP always has a few tricks up his sleeve that could get Wolves defenders in foul trouble.

If things are mucked up in the paint like the above numbers suggest, the importance of the Wolves making the "one extra pass" to an open shooter and converting could well be the secret sauce to unlocking offense against a very versatile defensive team. Isolation basketball that leans too heavily into the Wolves' 28th ranked assisting percentage will absolutely make this game feel like the Wolves are pushing a boulder uphill all night long.

The Knicks starting group of Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby and KAT is a rare starting group that is as versatile as the Wolves. If Kuminga can't go and Minnesota chooses to put Jaden McDaniels on Jalen Brunson, there are going to be a lot of matchup issues for the Wolves. Assuming LaMelo Ball takes Josh Hart, Dosunmo will shift to Bridges, leaving OG Anunoby with a tantalizing matchup with either a size advantage on Cody Williams, or a speed and athleticism advantage on Trey "Elite Rim Protector" Lyles.

While Dosunmo could be on Brunson duty instead McDaniels, the defensive scheme makes a whole lot more sense if Kuminga is good to go.

My prediction is all based on the X-Factor of Jonathan Kuminga's availability Thursday. If he plays, the Wolves win a physical back-and-forth defensive slug fest 106-102 where Kuminga can match physicality with OG Anunoby.

If he's out, the Wolves just won't have quite enough bodies to throw at the trio of Brunson, Bridges, and Anunoby, losing 116-106. Wait for Kuminga's game status to be announced then go place your bets as the outcome has already been foretold!

#2827. NFL Injury Report, Week 11: Latest news, updates for Kenneth Walker III, Brock Bowers and more players for fantasy football

It was a rough week for the New England Patriots over in Germany. As we look over the Week 11 NFL injury report, the Patriots are going to pop up quite a bit going into their bye. We also have five other teams on bye — the Packers, Seahawks, Browns, Falcons and Rams. Those teams will hopefully get healthier over that span.

Below, we'll go over the latest injury news, providing updates on key players for fantasy football.

Drake Maye, NE (ankle) — Out indefinitely

Geno Smith, NYJ (concussion/ankle) — Intends to play

Baker Mayfield, TB (lower leg) — Could miss Week 11

Maye: New England heads into its bye, though the season may be lost coming out of it. At this point, it's feared Maye has a fractured ankle and could need season-ending surgery. At the very least, he could miss multiple games or be placed on IR. It's almost helpful that New England is on bye in Week 11, as fantasy managers would already be looking for a Maye replacement or streaming option.

If Maye is done for the season, it's difficult to trust anyone on this offense. There are injuries and ailments everywhere, from A.J. Brown to Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The Pats are well behind the 8-1 Bills in the AFC East, though they are still in the wild-card picture. But if Maye is out, that outlook could change fast. If you have any skill-position player on New England, be sure to have contingency plans. This team could turn into a fantasy wasteland soon.

Mayfield: The Bucs are coming out of the Week 10 bye but may be without Mayfield. He suffered a lower-leg injury in Week 9's loss to Chicago, and the extra rest didn't appear to help. He missed Wednesday's practice, so we'll have to continue to monitor the situation. If Mayfield is out against Detroit in Week 11, Jalon Daniels, who started three games earlier in the season, would get another shot. With so many teams on bye and Maye managers searching for answers, Daniels is a potential option. Tampa Bay has a pretty soft schedule the rest of the season. Expect the Bucs to continue to ride the running game with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.

Woody Marks, HOU (concussion) — Ruled out

David Montgomery, HOU (groin) — Expected to return

Kyle Monangai, CHI (thumb/toe) — Expected to return

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, WAS (groin) — Could return from IR

Jonathon Brooks, CAR (core) — Could return from IR

Walker: The Chiefs added Walker to the injury report last Friday and he was swiftly ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. As a result, rookie Emmett Johnson thrived in lead-back duties, totaling 171 yards on 28 touches (six catches) with two TDs for 32.1 fantasy points. Reports suggest this will be a short absence for Walker, but he did miss practice Wednesday.

#2826. 'Hopefully he won’t be happy' - Harvey Barnes sends pointed warning to Bruno Guimaraes as Arsenal star prepares for hostile Newcastle reunion

Harvey Barnes has sent a clear message to former Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes, warning the Brazilian that his return to Tyneside with Arsenal will be anything but comfortable. The Magpies are desperate to kickstart their campaign after a stuttering run of form and view the arrival of the league leaders as the perfect opportunity to make a statement.

Premier League action resumes after the international break on Saturday evening with a high-stakes clash at St James' Park. The fixture marks Guimaraes' first appearance back on Tyneside since leaving Newcastle for Arsenal in a £75 million summer move.

Arsenal arrive in the north-east as commanding league leaders, having taken 27 points from a possible 30 to build a five-point cushion at the summit. Newcastle, meanwhile, have struggled at home, claiming just one win in five matches at St James' Park this campaign.

While Guimaraes' reception remains uncertain, he already enjoyed a memorable trip to the region earlier this season. He came off the bench to score against Sunderland, making an animated celebration despite receiving a hostile welcome from the home supporters.

Despite Arsenal's strong form, Barnes believes facing the table-toppers provides the exact spark his side require. Speaking ahead of the weekend clash, the winger insisted Newcastle relish testing themselves against elite opposition at home.

"In some ways I think it's a really good game for us," Barnes told Sky Sports. "Obviously you're testing yourself against the best and I think you've seen over the years when these challenges do come along, especially at St James' Park, we step up to them and really meet them head on. I feel like it's the kind of game we need coming off the break."

Seeing a former team-mate line up for a rival adds an extra edge to Saturday's meeting. However, Barnes brushed aside any sentimentality over Guimaraes returning in Arsenal colours, stressing Newcastle's focus remains firmly on the result.

"It's football. People leave and come back, Bruno is coming back in a different shirt," he added. "Hopefully he won't be happy at the end of the game with the result. It is what it is. We'll just go there and do our job."

Saturday evening's showdown carries major weight for both clubs as domestic action resumes. For Newcastle, toppling the division's pacesetters offers a prime chance to fix their sluggish home record and ignite their season.

Arsenal, meanwhile, face a stern examination on hostile territory as they look to protect their five-point lead at the Premier League summit.

#2825. Fernando Mendoza’s painful NFL debut could hold answers to next test vs Broncos

The best thing Fernando Mendoza has going for him Sunday in Denver might be the same thing the Broncos have going for them. Both sides got a good look at what happened to the Raiders rookie against Seattle.

Presumably, both sides hit the rewind button.

Fernando Mendoza (15) of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up before a game at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

For Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph, the attraction is obvious. The Seahawks sacked Mendoza six times in his first NFL start. Any coach with a rested pass rush and a home crowd willing to make life miserable for a visiting quarterback would be interested in how they went about it.

For Mendoza, the part worth rewinding might come a second or two before he hit the ground. What did he see when he came to the line? What changed when he got the ball? And where could he have gone with it once it did?

The Broncos present some big-time challenges in that regard.

"It's one of the top defenses in the league for a reason," Mendoza said. "So they are very good, they're very sound and I respect them a lot."

Coach Klint Kubiak is confident the rookie will process and adapt accordingly.

"His approach has been excellent since he got here," Kubiak said. "He's a competitor. It's his first NFL start. I thought he played well enough for us to win, especially in that first half, and we didn't close it out in the second half."

A week ago, those were questions he had to answer against Mike Macdonald's defense without the benefit of a single NFL start. On Sunday, there's at least a chance Joseph asks him something he's heard before.

Consider what Denver can take from the way Seattle made Mendoza account for pressure. A linebacker walking up to the line gives the quarterback something to think about. Put one in each gap alongside the center and now the quarterback and his protection have some decisions to make.

Michael Mayer of the Las Vegas Raiders avoids a tackle from Josh Jobe of the Seattle Seahawks in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

The beauty of it for Denver is that neither linebacker has to come. If Mendoza hurries a throw over the middle to beat a blitz and finds a linebacker dropping into the very window he picked out, Joseph will have gotten what he wanted without sending anybody extra.

So where's the opportunity for Mendoza? Start with what happens if that linebacker comes.

Somebody just vacated a valuable piece of real estate. A receiver breaking inside behind him can give Mendoza a throw he can make with his feet set, before the rush has much say in the matter. Six or 7 yards on first down would do wonders for an offense that spent too much of Sunday trying to figure out third-and-long.

There's a bigger throw available, too, if Denver decides to crowd the line and leave a cornerback outside with no safety behind him. That's a chance to give Tre Tucker a ball down the sideline. The trick is confirming the safety really did come down. Seattle gave Mendoza firsthand experience with how much a picture can change between the time a quarterback calls for the ball and the time it reaches his hands.

Getting Tucker involved would go a long way, especially if Brock Bowers' ankle injury keeps him on the sideline. Tucker's ability to stretch the field, and Mendoza's willingness to take some chances on those long throws, could help open things up for the run game and the short and intermediate passing game.

Tyler Linderbaum, left, Fernando Mendoza, center, and Jalen Nailor celebrate a touchdown in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images

"There are a lot of variables and what our coach always emphasizes making sure we're taking the positive gain," Mendoza said. "However, those deep shots and those explosives are what can help us win the game. And so, I mean, it's really play-by-play, and I look forward to taking a look at the shots we have this weekend."

Lost in those six sacks is a reason to believe Mendoza can make some of those throws. He completed 11 of 13 passes in the first half against Seattle and got the ball to eight receivers. He already knows what it feels like to take what an NFL defense gives him and move on to the next play.

Kubiak can help him get back to that. Give Mendoza an early throw on a moving pocket. Change where Denver's edge rushers expect to find him. And if the Broncos are getting upfield in a hurry, a well-timed screen gives those rushers an invitation to keep right on going.

Some of which requires a seamless process well ahead of the snap.

"I was very pleased with him getting out of the huddle, him making the correct checks, the correct calls," Kubiak said. "That's what he has shown in practice, his ability to do that and to be able to run the show that way. There's room for growth, but in his first start, I thought that he operated the game like he does in practice."

Of course, there's a limit to what anybody can draw up if the Raiders run for 65 yards on 24 carries again. Joseph had a bye week to study the Raiders. He hardly needed all of it to see the advantage in making Mendoza throw on downs when everyone in the stadium knows he has to.

Denver figures to make the rookie prove he can solve some of the problems Seattle put on tape. Fair enough.

But if the Broncos want to borrow from the Seahawks, Mendoza gets something out of the deal, too. Somewhere in all that film of what went wrong is a throw he'd love to have back.

"The most important thing is how he's playing the game. We'll coach up everything," Kubiak said. "But like I said, and like I told Fernando, I was pleased because of the preparation that he put in. The things that he did in practice showed up in the game, and he's going to have a lot of things to learn and grow from."

#2824. A Vice City rout: Heat defeat Bucks 137-130 in collab with ‘GTA VI'

A Vice City rout: Heat defeat Bucks 137-130 in collab with 'GTA VI' originally appeared on NBC Sports Boston

A loss on Vice City night never made sense.

The Miami Heat routed the Milwaukee Bucks 137-130 on Wednesday during a one-night-only promotional collaboration with Rockstar's "Grand Theft Auto VI," which launches in the U.S. at midnight Thursday.

Miami rolled out a new court at Kaseya Center with pink, blue and black colors matching its special-edition jersey. The words "Vice City" replaced the usual Heat logo in mid-court, while a "VI" with a palm tree featured in the corner of each paint.

Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo led the way for Miami in a night that meant a lot to both players. Antetokounmpo faced the team that drafted him for the first time, while Adebayo went head-to-head against former teammate Tyler Herro and Co.

Antetokounmpo posted a game-high 27 points on 7 of 11 shooting to go with 13 rebounds, nine assists, one steal and a block.

Adebayo followed suit with 26 points on 7 of 15 shooting to go with four rebounds, two assists and two steals. Adebayo dominated the first half, while Antetokounmpo took over in the second.

Davion Mitchell added 24 points on a hot 6 of 7 clip from long range to help Miami move to 9-6 after a slow start. Milwaukee fell to 1-14 as Kyle Kuzma scored 26 points to lead the team.

Milwaukee closed the gap in the final quarter once Miami pulled most of its starters, but the Heat had been in control since the end of the first.

Beyond the game, fans had access to a limited-edition Vice City merch and apparel collection at team shops throughout the arena. There were also unique cars on display for fans to see and a photo spot with the "VI" logo.

Vice City is the fictional name of the game's city that loosely represents Miami, while Leonida is the fictional Florida-inspired state the city is based in. Other prominent in-game locations are based on the Everglades and the Florida Keys.

"GTA VI" has been expected to be the biggest game of the decade since its initial trailer release in December 2023. The previous installment, based in a fictional Los Angeles and surrounding areas, released 13 years ago.

#2823. Nvidia’s Kress faces a divided workforce as some employees push for Huang’s return

The day before Colette Kress led her first earnings call as Nvidia's interim CEO, she did not want to talk about her predecessor, Jensen Huang.

"This is a new era for Nvidia," she told employees in an internal meeting on Monday, according to a person present, who spoke on the condition of anonymity. When someone brought up Huang, Kress quickly changed the subject, according to the person.

On Wednesday, Kress addressed the whole company at the first Nvidia all-hands meeting since the public chaos over Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and other reported relationships. And while Kress will be tasked with filling the leadership vacuum created by Huang's departure, she is also tamping down public calls to bring him back.

Huang himself weighed in with his first public statement Tuesday saying he would be "honored" to return to Nvidia.

Kress, who has served as the company's CFO since 2013, must steady employees and convince customers and investors that Nvidia can execute on its ambitious targets without the man who made them.

At Wednesday's meeting with staffers, Kress was joined by newly appointed board chair Harvey Jones as well as Ian Buck, who oversees Nvidia's hyperscale and high performance computing business, according to an attendee.

Kress' message was, "Let's move forward," said the person, who asked not to be named because the event was private.

Nvidia's leaders have made clear that the board does not plan to bring Huang back.

"The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen," Kress said in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer on Tuesday. "We want to grow in terms of everything that we need to do with our employees, our customers, our shareholders, and that is where we are going to focus moving forward."

Jones echoed the sentiment on Tuesday's earnings call. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," he said in opening remarks.

Nvidia declined to comment for this story.

Kress stressed on the earnings call that the company was focused on the workers who remain, who she said are "committed to doing their life's work at Nvidia." The company also reported better-than-expected earnings and seemed to calm investors' nerves, at least for the moment.

Some employees are telling a different story. Support for Huang's return is growing inside Nvidia, sources tell CNBC. An online petition circulating since the weekend has nearly 200,000 signatures, with more than 10,000 of them claiming to be current Nvidia employees. Nvidia currently has roughly 42,000 employees.

Outside Nvidia, Huang's reinstatement has been called for by at least two major investors and tech heavyweights such as Elon Musk, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. President Donald Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Huang return as CEO.

Several employees posted on X over the last few days, voicing support for Huang and calling for his return. One robotics engineer said the founder's departure led to his own decision to leave.

Another senior Nvidia employee, Nader Khalil, sent a letter to the company's board and top executives warning that failing to reinstate Huang could lead to a loss of "irreplaceable talent," according to The Wall Street Journal.

Huang was known for his deep day-to-day involvement in his company's operations, often responding directly to engineers and chiming in personally on technical projects.

Engineering employees, in particular, were "extremely devoted to him, almost like a demigod," according to a former Nvidia employee who was at the company for more than 15 years and spoke to CNBC on condition of anonymity.

Wednesday's all-hands is a standard meeting: Nvidia traditionally holds one on the morning after each quarterly earnings call, according to the former employee.

Still, the meeting is unlike anything the company has experienced. Employees told CNBC that they plan to share their grievances at the all-hands, though it wasn't clear ahead of time if they would be allowed to ask questions.

Huang took time to address employee questions during previous post-earnings all-hands meetings, the former Nvidia employee told CNBC, adding that Kress is "eager to demonstrate there's a new sheriff in town."

Kress ended Tuesday's earnings call with an upbeat message: "Our customers and our partners are with us. And employees are committed. We've got this."

— CNBC's Lora Kolodny contributed to this report.

#2822. Leclerc reveals what really happened in private meeting with Hamilton

Charles Leclerc has revealed fresh details about the meeting organised by Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur to resolve tensions between himself and Lewis Hamilton. The Monegasque explained that the discussions lasted around an hour, although the two drivers needed just a few minutes to clear the air.

Ferrari have faced a challenging period in recent races, with disagreements between their drivers attracting attention as the team continues its battle for second place in the Constructors' Championship.

Differences of opinion between Leclerc and Hamilton, particularly following the Mexican Grand Prix, have raised questions about the relationship between the two teammates.

Speaking to GPblog and other media ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, Leclerc insisted that the situation had been exaggerated and explained how Vasseur brought both drivers together to address their differences.

"Fred was definitely involved, as he was in the meeting, and he organised the meeting. So we were all three together, and the discussion went very well," Leclerc explained.

The Ferrari driver revealed that the atmosphere improved almost immediately once the three began talking: "As we've said, I think very, very quickly, we only had to speak. And after a few sentences already, the tension that was there wasn't there anymore, and it was all fine."

Leclerc also explained that the meeting lasted considerably longer than was necessary to resolve the disagreement, with the drivers eventually discussing other matters concerning Ferrari's future.

"It's not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour just because we had a good time and we started speaking about many other things in trying to bring the team and to help the team go forward. But the discussion about the tension was maybe five or ten minutes, and then the air was clean, and that's it."

Despite insisting that his relationship with Hamilton remains positive, Leclerc acknowledged that the two Ferrari drivers will not always share the same opinions.

"As I said, I think everything has been taken out of proportion. I'm kind of used to it now, driving for Ferrari for so many years, but things are very often taken out of proportion. Of course, the goal is not always to agree, and that will never happen. We can have different opinions, and that was the case, for example, in Mexico."

The Monegasque stressed that having different perspectives is not necessarily a problem, provided both drivers are willing to discuss their differences: "Just the fact of speaking solves tensions, and we're completely fine with it."

With Ferrari still fighting to secure second place in the Constructors' Championship, Leclerc also emphasised the importance of maintaining a united approach during the final races of the season.

"Second place in the Constructors' is important. It's also true that we've got a relatively big margin behind, which doesn't mean we need to minimise that, and we still have to work as a team. But what is really important for me now is to try and win before the end of the season and win a race."

Global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The company has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

In an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

"While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

Kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

The 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

"As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," said Mackay.

#2820. Tech outages are causing people to panic-buy. Costco is benefiting, Mizuho says

A series of tech outages has consumers stocking up on emergency supplies.

Costco sales are seeing a lift because of it, according to research firm Mizuho.

In the final week of October, Mizuho estimates, Costco's U.S. comparable sales, excluding gasoline, rose 11% to 12%, up from the normal 6% to 7% the first three weeks in October. Costco reported an 8.1% increase for the month. The firm said the stronger pace is continuing through November, as 21 of the 26 high-ticket generators it tracked on Costco's website sold out as of Sunday night.

Shares of Costco were roughly flat-to-lower in Wednesday morning trading at around $1,107 apiece.

"Consumer anxiety following the Microsoft Outlook outage, the ground stoppage for all U.S. airline flights, and apocalyptic concerns flaring up across social media have all contributed to increased emergency prep sales at COST," Mizuho analyst David Bellinger said in a research note Monday. Bellinger will appear on CNBC's "The Exchange" during the 1 p.m. hour.

On Thursday, an outage occurred in Microsoft's Outlook and Teams, and on Friday the Federal Aviation Administration halted departures nationwide. On Monday, a software outage at JPMorgan Chase caused banking transaction delays, and a system outage delayed United Airlines flights. The National Security Agency said Tuesday that the spy agency's communication network went down temporarily.

The outages appear to come amid a rush to recover software vulnerabilities uncovered by AI tools, and officials are saying there's no reason for panic.

Still, on TikTok and other social media platforms, posts urging people to stock up on food and supplies are gaining significant traction.

Mizuho raised its price target on Costco to $1,150 from $1,100 and kept its buy-equivalent outperform rating. The firm said U.S. comparable sales could grow more than 10% in November.

Mizuho also sees Walmart's Sam's Club benefiting from emergency preparedness sales as shoppers fill up their pantries, and for Home Depot and Lowe's as they buy home improvement emergency supplies.

At Costco, Mizuho will be watching whether the surge brought in new member sign-ups when the warehouse retailer reports its first quarter of fiscal 2027 on Dec. 10.

#2818. Two new housing reports point to bleak winter ahead, with record low sales

Two new reports on the housing market show activity slowing even more, after a September spike in mortgage rates sent it into a deep freeze.

Pending home sales in October dropped 4.7% month-over-month and were down 16.7% from October of last year, according to the National Association of Realtors. This is the lowest level in the index's 25-year history.

Analysts had been looking for a much smaller decline, likely because mortgage rates pulled back slightly in October, only to rise sharply again last week. The average rate on the 30-year fixed started October at 7.54% according to Mortgage News Daily and ended the month at 7.27%.

The pending count is based on signed contracts — people out shopping and signing deals during the month. It is therefore an indicator of future closed sales.

"Two consecutive months of record-low pending contracts point to very sluggish fourth-quarter home sales closings, and annual existing-home sales could be the lowest since the mid-1990s," said Lawrence Yun, NAR's chief economist in a release.

Regionally, sales were down across the nation with the sharpest drops in the South, which is usually busiest for sales and the West which is most expensive.

Another report released Wednesday showed gains in home construction in October but raised a red flag going forward. Single-family housing starts rose 4% from September, according to the U.S. Census, but were down 3.2% year over year. Building permits, an indicator of future construction, dropped 8.7% for the month and were down 12.9% from October 2025. That is the lowest level for permits since May 2020, the start of the Covid-19 pandemic.

"Builders are dealing with a litany of obstacles to selling homes, whether it's rising costs of land, labor, and materials, high financing costs, or weak buyer demand," wrote Joel Berner, senior economist at Realtor.com. "This month's data shows them slowing down activity at the top of their funnel, which will result in slower months of starts and completions later on."

The construction report follows a bleak reading on homebuilder sentiment, which fell to the lowest level in 14 years in November, on the monthly index from the National Association of Home Builders. Builders cited multiple challenges, including higher mortgage rates, higher costs for energy, materials and labor, as well as weaker consumer confidence.

#2817. Kellen Moore has run out of excuses in New Orleans

How many more embarrassing losses do the New Orleans Saints have to suffer before it's time to move on from Kellen Moore? Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Carolina Panthers at the Caesars Superdome should have been the final straw.

This was a game the Saints had every opportunity to win. Carolina committed an incredible 17 penalties for 152 yards, compared to just three penalties for 46 yards by New Orleans. The Panthers repeatedly shot themselves in the foot, yet the Saints couldn't take advantage of the opportunities in front of them.

Instead, New Orleans dropped to 3-6 and watched Carolina take sole possession of first place in the NFC South.

The Saints managed just 222 total yards, couldn't establish a running game even with Travis Etienne Jr. back and scored zero points in the first half. The running backs combined for just 24 yards on 17 carries, leaving Tyler Shough to shoulder far too much of the offensive responsibility.

At some point, the excuses have to stop. Injuries, personnel issues and growing pains can only explain so much. Moore is in his second season, and the same problems that plagued this team last year continue to show up every Sunday.

And now, it's starting to regress his promising young quarterback.

The Saints have struggled with preparation, offensive consistency, overall execution and closing out games during Moore's tenure. Those are the habits of a poorly coached football team, and Moore has repeatedly failed to find answers.

New Orleans needs a change. Sunday's loss was another reminder that this current regime just isn't getting the job done. The Saints cannot keep wasting opportunities in a division that remains wide open.

It's time for the Saints to stop pretending things are going to get better without making a change.

#2816. Dylan Harper ruled out against Clippers with “soreness”, more to come tomorrow

The Spurs had mostly avoided the injury bug that has buring through the league, until now. With injury report due for Thursday's match-up against the Clippers, the Spurs listed guard Dylan Harper as out due to "left hip soreness", but they will not have more information until tomorrow, according to San Antonio Express News' Tom Orsborn.

Harper suffered the injury in the final minute of last night's loss to the Pistons when he was running up the court and slipped, falling awkwardly and appearing to pull his groin. He stayed down for a bit before limping back to the locker room.

The Spurs will release more information when they hear from the medical staff tomorrow, and the amount of time Harper could potentially miss will depend on the severity of the injury. (It's rarely useful to listen to online doctors who are basing their opinions of the same videos we see, but most I've seen have ranged anywhere from 2-6 weeks, for whatever that's worth.)

He's joined by Tobias Harris (calf) and Jayden Quiantance (knee). Head coach Mitch Johnson remains noncommittal on a potential return timeline for Harris, and Quaintance told reporters at a turkey handout earlier in the day that he does not have a timeline either, but the goal is to get back to 100% and not rush things.

It's easy to assume that Julian Champagnie will once again return to the starting lime-up, which would give them the same line-up that made the Finals last season. The question of course will be back-up point guard. De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle may get their minutes more staggered, and Jordan McLaughlin could get some regular minutes. Another option would be to call Ja'Kobi Gillespie up from Austin.

#2815. Read Jim Cramer’s full interview with Nvidia’s Colette Kress: Demand, buybacks and China

Nvidia delivered another beat-and-raise quarter on Tuesday in the chipmaker's first report since Jensen Huang abruptly resigned as CEO last week amid a widening affair scandal. Revenue more than doubled from a year earlier, exceeding estimates by nearly $7 billion, while earnings topped expectations by 20 cents per share. An excellent quarter by almost any measure.

But investors remain skeptical about Nvidia's future without Huang, who famously founded the company at a San Jose Denny's in 1993. Shares fell 2.5% Wednesday, despite opening higher on the session. Will the company lose its smartest executives and engineers? Would Nvidia remain banker to the increasingly shaky neoclouds? Can it stay ahead of the competition?

On Tuesday night, Colette Kress sat down with CNBC's Jim Cramer shortly after delivering her first earnings call as interim CEO to answer these pressing questions and more.

This transcript has been edited for clarity.

Jim Cramer: After the bell, Nvidia reported earnings, and what a quarter it was. The stock jumped in after hours in response. This is the first time we are hearing from the company since its founder, Jensen Huang, stepped down as CEO last week. So let's check in with Colette Kress, Nvidia's longtime chief financial officer and now its interim CEO. Ms. Kress, welcome to "Mad Money."

Colette Kress: Thank you for having me, Jim. It's really great to see you.

Cramer: Thank you, Colette. The most important thing I heard tonight was that you increased your revenue growth forecast for next year. Previously, you said you would grow 70%. Now you're saying 75%, off of a higher base. How are you able to do that?

Kress: Thanks. Very, very important to understand how much our customers are interested in our compute infrastructure and how much they need the agentic solutions out there. So the most important thing that we have been seeing is just, again, a continuous growth in terms of the demand that's out there. But we also have been working in terms of our supply. So an increase in supply, working with all of our different suppliers, whether that be focusing in terms of what we need in terms of chips, what we need in terms of advanced packaging or memory, all of that is also coming together. We felt very confident, therefore, that we could establish that we will grow 75% year over year for fiscal year '28.

Cramer: Now, a lot of people have been saying that there was one man at this company. I've talked with you. There are another 49,000. How is the team holding up? Are there people who are saying, "You know what, this is not the Nvidia I know, I don't want to be there?" Is there a brain drain, as some people have told me?

Kress: Yeah, really great question. And remember, the company has been built on the perspective that employees see Nvidia as their life's work. And many of them have been here for decades, working with us from both a technology and a business-and-operations perspective. And now where we're standing is focusing on the business, focusing on getting all of that work done. And I had been working already with leadership. Leadership is supportive of everything we're doing and is standing up to help as we pull all employees and leaders together to move forward. But we have high confidence that our employees are definitely still working, still working with us, and enjoy really the work here at Nvidia.

Cramer: I have talked to you many times about the idea that the cheapest stock in the world is yours, and that's why you don't necessarily have to help other people buy your chips when you can just go buy your own stock. Where are you on buybacks versus lending aggressive amounts of money to, say, neoclouds? Because I think that the buybacks are a lot better for shareholders.

Kress: We have now been looking at the capability of making significant stock repurchases for our company. That is enabled by our significant growth and the cash we will have. During the quarter, we discussed increasing the amount of additional stock repurchases to more than $150 billion. That adds to a total amount at this point of $277 billion that we're going to be able to provide. We are completely committed to that. We do believe that that's something we're going to be able to complete all the way through, just to the end of 2027. So we are in line and continuing our stock repurchases for sure.

Cramer: OK. Thank you. That's important. And it's more aggressive than I thought. And I'm glad to hear that. Now, why are there many different reports about your company, and even about your accounting? I know you as the person who is in charge of the numbers. For instance, I read two different analysts who say you may be on the hook for about $530 billion in guarantees, which is worrisome because it could have a huge impact on your cash flow.  I heard a new disclosure tonight that made me feel like the on-the-hook number is not true.

Kress: Right now, our guarantees have been thoughtfully completed to date. And our guarantees are approximately about $118 billion, which includes one of the most important ones: a land, power, and shell backstop that we have with Portsmouth here in the United States, the best site for what we see, the future of multiple, multiple buildings working together to do that, about 4.5 gigawatts to do so. That is solely for Nvidia's infrastructure. It's working very well and is getting ready for all the builds it needs to do. And that is the most significant part of our guarantees. We will continue to do the best due diligence and thought regarding any additional guarantees that need to be done. That means we're going to be working with companies to make sure we understand where they are in terms of their land, power, shell builds, how they are doing in terms of getting ready for the compute, getting the capital that they need, and making sure that they have the end customer, the off-take that we'll need to complete that. So it's going to be a top priority. But we are all working together to make sure that we can support the most important ones that we think are running very well, and that's going to be a top priority for us.

Cramer: Speaking of priorities, from a lot of reporting, again, because I want to try to get all this stuff out. You were kind enough to come on and speak about anything unrehearsed. Based on much of the reporting over the last two weeks, it seems that the aggressive investments in the ecosystem, including some companies that are less than investment-grade, were a priority for your predecessor and his family members. I want to know if you were pushing back on those? And should we see less and expect less support for the ecosystem and more for the shareholders?

Kress: Our investments are an important part of the work we can do, focusing on a set of organizations that may be AI-native, maybe new types of companies starting, as well as helping those that want to build new types of models in the market. These are some of the areas that we focused on. But, yes, we're very disciplined in terms of how we think that through. There's a lot of discussion internally with a lot of the teams on what we think are the best ones that we want to do. And we're going to continue down that path to make sure we choose the right investments for us to work through going forward. But most importantly, these are companies in areas where we can see additional growth in AI. And I think those are important for us. But, again, stepping back to our business and how important our capital is going to be for procuring supply and getting ready for all of our employees as well, and all the work that we need to do from the engineering, that's going to be our top priority in terms of our use of capital to do so. So that's what I think is the most important.

Cramer: You are in a very competitive situation. For instance, AMD has a product that's a GPU that is much touted, and they think it can be moved in quicker. I know that some of the hyperscalers are very good at developing their own chips, which makes some people say, "Wait a second. Is what's really happening that Nvidia is supporting some companies that may not be, let's say, investment-grade or the kind of customer you would want — neoclouds — because it's losing business from the traditional hyperscalers and their shares are going down. Is that true?

Kress: Interesting statement, but no, it is not true. If we want to think about where we are with our hyperscalers, they are right now feverishly looking for more focus on the compute we have available. I have seen already with many of these contacting me and saying, " Great to see everything intact. Great to see that there's more supply. I need more demand." So they are all with us. And remember, there's a reason why. That is an amazing type of architecture that has been built through so much work with the different types of engineers. It is the most durable, fungible, and performant type of infrastructure out there. The idea that anything is changing among our customer types is just not true. They are all still with us. And we have a very deep breadth of different customers. And I think that's important to understand. These will be needed for all the different organizations overseas as well. They're going to want to say, "How do I have someone building a different type of data center overseas that they would want to see as well?" So I do believe it is appropriate to have different types of organizations that will be using this type of compute. But keep in mind, the stock, the amount of different types of customers, is broad. And we are going to continue to focus on that.

Cramer: This level of demand makes me ask you a particular question, which is that, if you were no longer allowed or wanted to ship into Southeast Asia for fear that it might end up in China, the flow back would not overwhelm pricing and drive it down, but instead would just help sate some of demand, but not all the demand? You do not need Southeast Asia to make or advance your numbers?

Kress: Well, what we are always working on is: Where do we feel we can provide the demand to our customers? We are always very, very cautious in terms of where we will be shipping to and making sure, yes, the data center is ready, and whether or not we also know that off-take and we know that customer piece of it. That is part of our process, and we will continue there. Let's just remember what we are right now in terms of our shipments to China. Our shipments to China are approximately about 10%. But that is our gaming business. That is our automotive business. That is our workstation business that is going there. As you also saw us announce, we would only have the licensed H200s [Nvidia's data center GPUs], and those went to China within this last quarter. And we are no longer shipping H200 at all, let alone not shipping it to China. So we are very careful and will continue to focus on that.

Cramer: I do want to ask you something that I think was a question that was handled by the board, but I didn't necessarily get an answer that I felt satisfactory. I understand, and have heard, that the chairman of the board says the board does not intend to ask Jensen Huang to return as CEO. But I have to say that perhaps the board would consider, after a thorough investigation — which I do not believe they did, frankly — that Jensen's value to our nation's technology, as expressed by our president today, could lead him to do something else for you. Perhaps a chief technologist or an ambassador for Nvidia's dominance who would not run afoul of either the SEC or anything done by Commerce or the Secretary of the Treasury.

Kress: Jensen resigned from his position with Nvidia, and the board accepted his resignation. The board has determined that they will not reinstate Jensen. And that is our statement and what the board has decided to do. We want to think about growing our business right now. We want to grow in everything we do with our employees, our customers, and our shareholders, and that is where we will focus moving forward.

Cramer: Do you think that it's possible that the two-way compute market project that Jensen started, that was going to be done with Goldman, with BlackRock, with Apollo, will continue? That's $500 billion in financing to make it happen the way we think it should.

Kress: Those financing funds are very important to us. We announced that they will continue to work with us, and their continued assistance with many of these companies that may be just shy of investment-grade and want to explore financing options; we're excited that they are part of this work. They are part of helping us create an asset class of our systems as well. No other company has that durability and fungibility outside of Nvidia. So they are important partners. We're going to continue working to help many of the different companies get the financing that they may want to do and the efficiency of that financing.

Cramer: You cleared up many questions for us tonight, and I really appreciate it. I know there are a lot of people who, I think, say a lot of things about your company that aren't true. I want to thank you, Colette Kress, who's been true north for me for many, many years, for as long as we've known each other. I want to say — I would say congratulations on the interim CEO. I'm glad you were on our show tonight, and I hope those who want to understand what kind of company this really is go back over what she said. It's quite different from what I hear every day on Wall Street. Colette Kress is the former CFO, and interim CEO, and it was great to have you on the show. Thank you, Colette.

#2813. Boston Celtics (11-3) at Denver Nuggets (7-5) Game #15 11/18/26

Boston Celtics (11-3) at Denver Nuggets (7-5)Wednesday, November 18, 20269:30 PM ETRegular Season Game #15 Road Game #8TV: ESPN, NBCSB, Altitude SportsRadio: 98.5 Sports Hub,92.5 Altitude Sports Radio, Sirius XMBall Arena

The Celtics begin a 4 game road trip in Denver to take on the Nuggets. This is the first of 2 games between these two teams this season. They will face off again in Boston on February 9. The Celtics were 0-2 last season against the Nuggets. They are 62-42 overall, all time, against the Nuggets and they are 21-31 in games played in Denver.

With their loss to the Magic, the Celtics have dropped to 2nd in the East, half a game behind the first place 76ers. They are 2 games ahead of 3rd place Detroit. They are 5-2 on the road and 8-2 in their last 10 games. They are 1-1 against Western Conference teams. They are coming off a loss in their last game.

The Nuggets are 8th in the West, 4 games behind 1st place San Antonio and 1.5 games behind 6th place Portland. Surprisingly, they have a better road record than home. They are 2-3 at home and 4-2 on the road. They are 6-4 in their last 10 games and they are 2-0 against Eastern Conference opponents. They are coming off a loss in their last game.

The Nuggets have made a few changes since last season but no major changes. They have added free agents Marvin Bagley III, Alpha Diallo, and Tyus Jones. They signed Bryce Hopkins, Ryan Nembhard, and Cam Whitmore to 2-Way contracts. They added Trevon Brazile with the 35th pick in the draft. They lost Tim Hardaway, Jr, Jonas Valanciunas, Bruce Brown, Jalen Pickett and Payton Watson.

After this game, the Celtics will continue their West coast trip through Sacramento, Golden State, and Washington. They then play one game at home against Atlanta before playing at San Antonio and Dallas. Then it's home against Charlotte before a game at Brooklyn. Next they have a 7 game home stand against Washington twice, Utah, Detroit, Portland, Miami and Cleveland.

After the Celtics, the Nuggets will host Houston before one game at Chicago and a game at home against Dallas. Then they have a 6 game road trip through Utah, Toronto, Detroit, Philadelphia, Utah (again), and Portland. Then they host Atlanta and the Lakers before playing at the Clippers, Lakers and Golden State, They then host Indiana and play a home and home series vs Minnesota.

I'm going to guess that the Celtics will be starting their regular starting lineup of Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum and Neemias Queta. Of course, Joe can always surprise us with an unexpected change at any time. I'm going with the Denver starting line up of Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon and Nikola Vucevic from their Game Notes.

The Celtics have no one on their injury report at this time. Since they aren't playing back to back games, they should not have to rest anyone. The Nuggets have just Julian Strawther on their injury report. He was was diagnosed with a left knee sprain in a preseason game and has yet to make his debut in the regular season.

Probable Starting Matchups PG: Derrick White vs Jamal Murray

Key Matchups Neemias Queta vs Nikola JokicJokic is has won 3 MVP's and is in the conversation for MVP every season for a reason. He is averaging 24.1 points, 10.9 rebounds, 8.9 assists, 1.1 blocks and 1.8 steals per game. He is shooting 51.6% from the field and 26.0% from beyond the arc. Over his career, against the Celtics, he has averaged 23.1 points, 10.8 rebounds 6.9 assists and 1.2 steals per game. He is a handful and the Celtics need to try to slow him down by any means necessary and especially keep him out of the paint.

Derrick White vs Jamal MurrayMurray is averaging 26.1 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 6.0 assists per game. He is shooting 53.5% from the field and 47.1% from beyond the arc. Over his career against the Celtics, he has averaged 19.8 points, 4.9 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 1.1 steals. Honorable MentionJordan Walsh vs Christian BraunBraun is averaging 12.6 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 2.3 assists and 2.2 steals per game. He is shooting 48.3% from the field and 35.2% from beyond the arc. Over his career against the Celtics, he has averaged 7.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.5 assist per game.

Keys to the GameDefense – Defense is the key to winning every game. The Celtics are 2nd with a defensive rating of 106.1. The Nuggets have a defensive rating of 114.9, which is 20th. The Celtics are 5th in the league with an offensive rating of 118.2 and the Nuggets are 10th with an offensive rating of 115.1. The Celtics have made defense their identity but against the Magic, their effort on that end was lacking. They need to go all out every game on the defensive end to win this and every game.

Rebound – Rebounding is another key to winning every game. The Celtics are 10th in the league, averaging 44.9 rebounds per game. The Nuggets are 25th in the league with 41.7 rebounds per game. Rebounding takes effort and the Celtics have to work harder to grab rebounds to limit the Nuggets second chance points and fast breaks. The Celtics are 7-1 when they have more rebounds than their opponents. They have to put in the effort to beat the Nuggets on the boards.

Effort and Energy for 48 Minutes – The Celtics must be the more aggressive team. They have to fight for loose balls, defend aggressively, be aggressive in driving to the basket, and just play harder than the Nuggets for the entire game. They have to be the team that wants it more and plays like it. They especially have to begin the game with energy and not allow the Nuggets to race out to a big lead and then, they can't let up throughout the game. They also have to come out strong in the 3rd quarter and play hard until the final buzzer. They allowed the Magic to play harder than them, especially in the 4th quarter and they can't do that in this game if they want to win it.

Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics need to keep moving the ball to find the open man. Doing that makes it much harder to guard them. However, they have to be careful with their passes and they also need to be careful when they dribble the ball and not drive into a crowd and turn the ball over. The Celtics are usually very good at taking care of the ball but at times they lose focus and get sloppy. They can't afford to do that against the Nuggets.

X-FactorsMile High on the Road– It's tough to win in Denver because of the altitude that the teams are playing at. Denver is called the Mile High City because it is 5,280 feet above sea level. Nuggets players are used to the altitude but visiting teams often struggle with playing there and often are fatigued before the end of the game. It is a very unique home court advantage. The Celtics also have to shake off the distractions of travel and playing in front of a hostile crowd and play hard and play their game.

Officiating – I know that I say this every game, but the officiating can always be an x-factor. Every crew calls the game differently whether they call every little ticky tack foul or they let a lot of contact go and let the teams play. We have already seen games where the officiating made a difference in the outcome, both good and bad. The Celtics have got to adjust to the way the game is being called and not let the calls affect their focus or their play. The Celtics also have to be aware of the new points of emphasis for this season and try to avoid flopping, off‑arm push‑offs, reckless closeouts, delays before free throws, and illegal screens.

#2812. Is Apple the safe haven investors think it is? Here's a way to trade it with less risk

For months, Apple has been the undisputed haven of the technology sector. As the industry grappled with the brutal reality of Nvidia's post-Huang future, investors blindly rotated into Apple, comforting themselves with the narrative that the Cupertino giant was uniquely immune to speculative overspending on artificial intelligence.

While peers bled capital into server farms and data centers. At almost 37x forward earnings estimates, the stock is now priced for perfection, fully valued at precisely the moment the rest of the market is beginning to see multiples contract aggressively. Investors tend to huddle in the shelter of perceived safe havens, but that perceived safety can crack quickly in an adverse news cycle, as Nvidia shareholders recently learned.

One part of the news cycle finally caught up to Apple.

We've recently witnessed a bizarre parade of catastrophic system failures: the massive Microsoft outage, the FAA grounding flights, and cascading disruptions across major banking networks. Through it all, Apple was immune. Until today, when a widespread outage struck, knocking out iCloud, Apple Pay, and core support systems. The official explanation? Yet another internal update gone wrong.

It's undeniably odd how all these major tech infrastructure failures are being chalked up to routine upgrades, all clustering around the exact same narrow timeframe. Without venturing too far into the conspiratorial, the sheer coincidence of these cascading digital blackouts suggests more systemic fragility than we may have realized. That's one thing at less than 10x forward earnings, as Nvidia is, or even at a market multiple. But Apple is twice as expensive as the S&P.

Technically, Apple is balancing on a knife's edge. Shares have been relentlessly hugging the upper end of several channel-based technical indicators, such as the Bollinger Band. Apple has been priced at a steep premium for being immune to what ails other struggling stocks, but is now demonstrating similar vulnerabilities. Investors should ask themselves: what's the upside? That Apple trades at more than 40x forward earnings? 45x? Even at that rich multiple, that would represent only 18-19% upside from here. If the market suddenly decided that Apple's premium to the market would be just 50%, instead of 100%, that would be less than 28x forward earnings, a nearly 27% haircut to the current share price.

Despite the high multiple, options prices are low versus the market. Market implied volatility is well above average (around the 93rd percentile). Apple implied volatility is actually just below the 1-year average. The price of index options is in the 98th percentile relative to Apple options.

Because the stock is nominally expensive (translation? The share price is high in dollar terms), buying outright naked puts is highly capital-intensive. This is exactly where a put spread makes sense. By buying an at-the-money or slightly out-of-the-money put and simultaneously selling a lower-strike put, traders can dramatically reduce the upfront capital cost. More importantly, this structure blunts the negative impact of theta, or time decay, ensuring you don't bleed premium while waiting for the technical breakdown to materialize. Furthermore, taking advantage of the natural put skew—where further out-of-the-money puts trade at relatively higher implied volatility—lets you finance your bearish bet efficiently by selling that inflated premium.

Apple's historic premium is built on a foundation of immunity to the chaos infecting the rest of the market. Today's outage proved the company may be more vulnerable than investors appreciate.

(Programming note: I will be live on cnbc.com at 2:30 talking about all of this. Be sure to tune in.)

#2811. Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in new businesses

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:

Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly important sources of transaction revenue, while the company has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney
