#2740. Celtics announce starting lineup against Denver Nuggets

DENVER — The Celtics will start Derrick White, Jordan Walsh, Paul George, Jayson Tatum, and Neemias Queta when they face the Denver Nuggets on Wednesday.

Queta is coming off his first rest night of the season, a Monday night Celtics loss to the Orlando Magic, which snapped the team's 6-game win streak. The Celtics struggled without him, with Luka Garza starting and Mitchell Robinson and Chris Cenac Jr. playing backup minutes.

But, Monday was more of an anomaly than a typical Boston performance; the Celtics have the fourth-best offensive rating and second-best defensive rating in the league. Only the Minnesota Timberwolves (104.0) have a better defensive rating than Boston (106.1).

And, before tip-off, Nuggets head coach David Adelman praised the Celtics' defensive versatility.

"I think it's been the most underrated thing about them," Adelman said. "Queta is a very active big…Obviously Derrick's always been a good defender. All those guys, they bought into what they do."

Adelman also said he thought people overlooked how good the Celtics might be this season after Jaylen Brown was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Paul George and draft compensation.

"I thought quietly what was maybe misunderstood was: everybody else is coming back. Tatum was back, all that shooting's back. It's not like Pritchard's in the trade, and there's a lot of really good players. Jaylen Brown's an all-time great player, but their team core is back."

The Celtics are 11-3 entering the season; the Nuggets are 7-5.

The Nuggets will start Jamal Murray, Christian Braun, Cam Johnson, Aaron Gordon, and Nikola Jokic.

Pregame, Joe Mazzulla was asked about limiting Nikola Jokic — and explained there's no easy way to do it.

"You have to defend them with your offense," Mazzulla said. "You can't play inefficient offense. You can't allow them to get more shots than you. You can't turn the ball over. If you get into a close game, you have to pick your poison. He is a very good player, and he has the ability to put pressure on every single coverage. He's seen every single coverage. So it's not about stopping him. It's about containing him and winning on the margins. We can't put him on the free throw line. You can't give up offensive rebounds. You can't give up back cuts, and you have to play efficient offense. Guys like that test the margins, and you have to play two-way basketball. You have to be able to attack them so that you can defend them. And you wouldn't guard them the same way down five as you would tied, as you would up five, because of their ability to put stress on multiple coverages. So you have to play well-balanced basketball against a team like this tonight, and the margins are super important. You start giving up back cuts, offensive rebounds, fouls; you're not going to be able to guard them in the half-court, so you've got to be disciplined on both ends of the floor."

#2739. Todd Bowles: Baker Mayfield's made progress, decision on playing to come on Friday

Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield missed practice on Wednesday with a foot injury, but the team hasn’t made a decision on his availability for Sunday’s game against the Lions.

Mayfield suffered the injury during Tampa’s Week 9 loss to the Bears and he recuperated during the bye week. Head coach Todd Bowles said that has allowed him to improve enough for the team to leave the door open for him to play this weekend.

Rookie Jalon Daniels worked with the first team on Wednesday. Easton Stick was signed to the active roster and the Bucs also added Cooper Rush to the practice squad this week.

#2738. Sean Mannion to continue calling offensive plays for Eagles, Joe Milton to remain at QB

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said that the team would talk about changes to roles and responsibilities on the coaching staff during their bye week, but he said on Wednesday that they decided against any major ones.

That means offensive coordinator Sean Mannion will continue calling the team’s offensive plays when they face the Steelers this week. Sirianni explained why he’s staying the course at a Wednesday press conference.

“I think he’s really smart. I think he has a great football mind,” Sirianni said, via a transcript from the team. “He thinks through everything. I think one thing I always value about him is [that] anybody can come and give a play and say, ‘Hey, I want to do this, or I want to do that.’ I think he just has a really good monotonous approach to figuring out everything that could potentially happen in that situation, what the downfalls are, what the upside is and whether we move forward with some of those things. I think that just speaks to the detail that he has. It hasn’t gone well enough for any of us this year offensively. That’s coaches, that’s players. We all have things that we need to do better, but I do love that approach that he has with that. As we looked at some of our schemes that he’s brought in, some of those have been really, really good. It has to be better as a whole without getting too much into the specifics of what those are. We just need to build on that.”

Mannion will be sending the play calls in to quarterback Joe Milton for the second straight game. He was 18-of-34 for 169 yards while running nine times for 64 yards and losing a fumble in a Week 9 loss to the Giants.

“He works extremely hard with everything,” Sirianni said. “Really love his approach, like his personality, but I really appreciate his approach to how he goes through everything.”

The loss to the Giants was the seventh in a row for the Eagles. They’ll try to avoid their first eight-game slide since 2012 this week.

#2737. 2027 UFL Draft tracker, results, top prospects as Diego Pavia finds landing spot

The 2027 UFL Draft has arrived, and football fans have one question on their minds heading into the event. Where will former Vanderbilt quarterback Diego Pavia land?

Pavia announced in October he was planning to join the UFL ahead of its 2027 season. The 2025 Heisman Trophy runner-up will instantly become one of the spring football league's biggest stars and will look to prove to all the teams that passed on him in the 2026 NFL Draft that he deserves a chance to play professionally.

While Pavia is the marquee name in the 2027 UFL Draft's player pool, there are plenty of other players with whom football fans will be familiar. A total of 120 players will be selected across the two-day, 15-round event that will help fill out the rosters of the UFL's eight current teams.

Of course, not every player selected is guaranteed to play in the UFL. The spring football draft is a rights draft, meaning teams retain the rights to negotiate with selected players should they choose to play in the UFL.

Still, spring football fans will be eager to see the crop of talent that could be poised to enter the UFL ahead of its 2027 season.

USA TODAY Sports is tracking the results of the 2027 UFL Draft. Follow along with the latest picks and a breakdown of the top prospects available in this year's draft class.

Pavia finished as the runner-up in the 2025 Heisman Trophy voting and signed with the Baltimore Ravens after going undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft. He was released before the preseason and now will look for a shot to play in the UFL.

Martinez played spring football in 2024, when he won the USFL MVP while a member of the Birmingham Stallions after throwing for 1,748 yards, 15 touchdowns and three interceptions while adding a league-high 528 rushing yards and three scores on the ground. He parlayed that opportunity into a chance with the New York Jets and has spent the last three NFL seasons with the Jets, San Francisco 49ers and Seattle Seahawks.

Currently, Martinez is on the Seahawks' practice squad. It isn't clear whether the 26-year-old will look to return to spring football, but his dual-threat ability will certainly make him a hot commodity should he decide to do so.

Steele went undrafted out of UCLA in 2024 but quickly earned a role in the Kansas City Chiefs' backfield. He totaled 183 yards on 56 carries as a rookie but has only handled one touch, a 4-yard reception, over his last two years with the Chiefs and the Philadelphia Eagles.

Steele (6-0, 228 pounds) is a big-bodied bruiser who runs with great physicality. That could make the 24-year-old a goal-line hammer at the UFL level.

Floriea may not be a household name, but he endeared himself to Cleveland Browns fans during the 2025 and 2026 preseasons. The Kent State product notched a combined seven receptions for 125 yards and three touchdowns across four games of preseason action with the Browns.

Floriea spent the 2025 season on Cleveland's practice squad but failed to earn a spot despite a strong performance in the 2026 preseason. The 25-year-old is small at 5-8, 180 pounds, but his hands and separation skills could make him a quality UFL pass-catcher.

Cunningham, a former Louisville quarterback, began his career as a signal-caller for the Baltimore Ravens and New England Patriots. However, in recent seasons, he transitioned to the receiver position and played one game at the position for the Detroit Lions.

Cunningham, 28, has never attempt a pass nor made a catch at the NFL level, but his dual-threat skill set would make him an intriguing fit for the UFL.

Cunningham isn't the only Louisville product who could draw interest in the UFL draft. Thrash, a 2024 fifth-round pick by the Browns, is in the player pool, and UFL teams would love to get their hands on the speedy 6-0, 190-pound receiver.

Thrash recorded 13 receptions for 129 yards across two seasons with the Browns. He also spent two weeks on the Las Vegas Raiders' practice squad during the 2026 NFL season.

Bell was a seventh-round pick by the Patriots in the 2024 NFL Draft after he enjoyed a standout career at South Carolina and Florida State. Bell made just two catches for 20 yards with the Patriots, but he showed off his upside as a senior with the Seminoles, recording 39 receptions for 503 yards and two touchdowns.

Bell is a bit short for a tight end at 6-2, 241 pounds, but he has a well-rounded skill set that could make him hard to cover for UFL defenders.

Wright's name will be familiar to college football fans, as he tried to become one of the first players to see action with an NFL team and return to the college level. His efforts were denied, leaving Wright in limbo after the Browns waived him and LSU chose not to add him to its roster.

Wright (6-4, 246 pounds) may yet get a chance to play professionally in the UFL. The Ole Miss product had 39 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns his final season with the Rebels and it's easy to see him developing into a mismatch threat in the spring game.

Pete, like Wright, made headlines during the 2026 NFL preseason. The Kentucky product spent time with the Dallas Cowboys, becoming the first NFL player from the Navajo Nation and earning rave reviews for a locker room speech following Dallas' preseason win over the Arizona Cardinals.

At 6-9, 309 pounds, Pete looks the part of a high-upside, developmental offensive lineman. Developing in the UFL could help him eventually emerge as a contributor thanks to his size alone.

Martin-Rhodes is one of the highest-drafted former NFL players in the 2027 UFL Draft's player pool. He was a third-round pick by the Lions in 2023 but was never quite able to carve out a role during his NFL stops with the Lions and Pittsburgh Steelers.

Martin-Rhodes has just six career tackles and no sacks. The 27-year-old will look to show off his abilities as a run stuffer behind his 6-5, 330-pound frame.

Heat's Bam Adebayo lets 'great karma' handle the Tyler Herro feud fallout appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

MIAMI – With the Miami Heat hosting Tyler Herro and the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night, the reunion was just one of the many storylines spinning out of the home team's 137-130 win. As Bam Adebayo and the Heat sported the "Grand Theft Auto VI" (GTA VI) styled jerseys on Wednesday, the team's captain would give insight into the relationship with his former teammate.

The contest would feature the stylish GTA-inspired "Vice City" jerseys, with some fans waiting out in the rain to buy one as it reportedly sold out in 90 minutes, and also Giannis Antetokounmpo facing his former team for the first time since the trade. However, no storyline was more palpable in Miami than the matchup against Adebayo and Herro, who were teammates for seven seasons with the Heat until the two were in a physical altercation in July during Summer League.

Stemming from social media activity connected to Herro, such as critiquing Adebayo in private messages, like one reading "should an elite defender be making 60 million a year? Answer that," the captain would respond. Approaching him at a practice court and reportedly punching Herro, there's no denying that the two former leaders of Miami ended their relationship ugly.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Whether it was before the game, during the game, or after the game, the two didn't acknowledge one another, though Herro embraced other former teammates throughout the night. Adebayo was asked if he spoke to Herro at any point and if there's disappointment with how their friendship deteriorated; he expressed that he is "on to the next thing" and has "great karma."

"No, I didn't get to talk to him," Adebayo said. "You know, usually when I'm in competitive mode, I don't really do a lot of talking anyway. Far as like how far it goes, I mean, you kind of see, obviously, the history of it. But some of that you see how you feel. So, to me, I'm on to the next thing. You know, I feel like I got great karma, and that's how I live my life. That's why I've been so blessed. You know, with the things that I've gotten. So, I just kind of give it to God and keep it pushing."

Herro spoke about the relationship with Adebayo at Wednesday morning's shootaround, saying how it's "human nature" for relationships to change, and praised his former teammate for his competitiveness.

There was no doubt a competitive energy from Adebayo, as he recorded 26 points on seven of 15 shooting from the field to go along with four rebounds, two assists, and two steals. As for Herro, he scored eight points on four of 11 shooting from the field, missing all five of his three-point attempts, with four assists and two rebounds.

Adebayo was also asked if there was a sense of closure from the game in facing Herro, but the 29-year-old emphasized that he has "been moved past that."

"I'm not one of the people that hold grudges," Adebayo said. "Like I said, I give it to God, and I move on. You know that's why I feel like I've been blessed with situations I've been in and to be able to obviously play in this game and be a part of something historic like GTA night. For me, it's not worrying about the negativity. It's worrying about how we can build this basketball team and keep stacking up these wins."

Herro, along with Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, and Kasparas Jakucionis, were honored with a tribute video before the game. Though, when Herro's name was announced in Milwaukee's starting lineup, there were boos, and it continued throughout the game as he continued to get touches with the ball.

Jakucionis was the second-leading scorer on Milwaukee with 20 points to go along with five assists and three rebounds, as Jaquez finished with 10 points, five assists, and two rebounds. Looking at Ware, he recorded 11 points with three rebounds.

As for the other side of the blockbuster trade in the summer, Antetokounmpo had 27 points with 14 rebounds and nine assists, while Bobby Portis Jr. had nine points and three rebounds.

All in all, the Heat handled business on Wednesday night against the Bucks, as it marks their sixth straight win, and the team are now winners in eight of their last 10 games. While there were storylines regarding Herro and the other former Miami players returning and Antetokounmpo facing his former team, Adebayo said that the game "is bigger than that."

"Glad we got the win. You know, obviously this is…it's kind of a reunion for a lot of people, but you know, from our side, this is bigger than that," Adebayo said to ClutchPoints. "You know, we had a complete setup of GTA and 2K, one night only. So for us, it was really about getting that win."

At any rate, the next time the Heat face the Bucks will be on Jan. 28, when Antetokounmpo returns to Milwaukee for the first time since the trade. Looking short-term, Miami looks to extend the winning streak to seven games on Sunday when the mighty Oklahoma City Thunder come into town.

#2735. A trading strategy to ride out the Nvidia uncertainty and generate income in the process

Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation has sent shockwaves through the tech sector, dragging Nvidia's (NVDA) stock down roughly 30% since Oct. 6. The market despises uncertainty, and losing a visionary founder, particularly one without a well-telegraphed succession plan, makes it worse.

However, for opportunistic investors, this panic has made the stock cheaper (obviously) while options have become significantly more expensive. Trading in the $160s, Nvidia's valuation has taken a big haircut, yet its underlying business fundamentals remain largely intact. While Huang was the architect of Nvidia's AI dominance, the company's moat — superior GPUs, the CUDA software ecosystem, and networking expertise — does not walk out the door with him. The company's structural advantage in the global artificial intelligence rollout persists.

Buying good companies at a discount is investing 101, but the current market dynamics may do something else for those who use options.  Huang's departure guarantees that Nvidia will be operating under a cloud of transition for the foreseeable future. Executing a permanent CEO search while navigating global regulatory scrutiny takes time. Consequently, Nvidia's implied volatility (IV)—the market's pricing of expected future price swings — has spiked to highs not seen since the tariff tantrum in the first half of 2025, and this elevated IV is highly likely to persist for several months as the leadership drama slowly unfolds.

This prolonged period of high implied volatility can be a goldmine for option sellers, specifically those executing options overlays such as covered call strategies. When you buy NVDA shares at these depressed levels and simultaneously sell out-of-the-money call options against your position, the premiums you collect are directly tied to IV. Because fear and transition-related uncertainty have dramatically inflated these option prices, the income generated from selling covered calls is now significantly higher than usual.

This lowers the risk profile of holding the stock considerably over time. Consistently collecting these inflated premiums systematically lowers your overall cost basis in the underlying shares. If the stock trades sideways or recovers slowly during the CEO search, you are generating an outsized cash yield on a stagnant asset. If the stock experiences further downside turbulence, the heavy premium income acts as a substantial downside buffer, meaningfully reducing the strategy's overall risk over time.

By deploying a persistent covered call strategy, investors can leverage the exact fear driving the stock down to generate robust, risk-reducing income while maintaining exposure to the undeniable future of AI.

#2733. Syracuse Benched Kiyan Anthony in Near-Upset vs. Cornell

NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 15: Kiyan Anthony #7 of the Syracuse Orange looks on ahead of the game against the St. John's Red Storm at Madison Square Garden on November 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)

Kiyan Anthony has had a revival to start this season for the Syracuse Orange. After a freshman season of inefficiency and uncertainty about his viability as a high-major player, Carmelo's son was great in SU's first four games this campaign.

And then came Wednesday night in the JMA Wireless Dome against the Cornell Big Red, a trap game against a sneaky-good Ivy League program with a potent, fast-paced, cut-heavy offense.

Kiyan wasn't given a single second on the court in the second half.

He spent most of his time with a towel either around his neck or atop his head, seemingly knowing his chances of getting in the game were declining by the second.

Syracuse held off the upset bid, and head coach Gerry McNamara will be hoping his lesson sinks in with Kiyan.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 15: Kiyan Anthony #7 of the Syracuse Orange looks on ahead of the game against the St. John's Red Storm at Madison Square Garden on November 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)

Kiyan's defense wasn't good enough in the first half for McNamara to trust him in a close game in the second half.

Multiple times, Anthony was caught ball-watching and got beat on backdoor cuts.

Against a Cornell offense that's all about pace, space and movement, Syracuse couldn't afford lapses on that end of the floor.

McNamara said in a postgame TV interview with the ACC network broadcast that included Jim Boeheim as the color commentator that he simply stuck with guys in the second half who he felt were getting it done on defense.

Boeheim agreed that Kiyan just hadn't been sharp enough defensively early in the game to play later on.

Boeheim also made the point during his postgame commentary that a game like this could help Syracuse more than a 40-point blowout.

It's not that SU wants to be firing at less than full capacity, but the reality is that there'll always be off nights, and they're a chance to learn lessons.

Kiyan specifically can learn lessons about defense, but there are opportunities for the Orange to grow all over the floor.

Sometimes when an opponent is insanely overmatched, those lessons aren't learned.

Cornell showed Syracuse some of its flaws. It'll be up to the Orange to figure out how to address them going forward.

#2730. This CT girls soccer team advanced to the championship game for the first time since 2019

NAUGATUCK – It's been seven years since the Glastonbury girls soccer team has advanced to a state championship game.

It's been eight years for the Guardians' coach Mark Landers.

The Glastonbury girls won their last title – their fifth since 2011 – in 2019. Landers coached the boys team for 20 years, winning eight state titles (his last in 2018), before taking over the girls team in 2021.

And now they're going back to the finals. Glastonbury defeated Ridgefield 2-1 Wednesday night in a Class LL semifinal girls soccer game at Naugatuck High.

"It feels great," Glastonbury senior Zoey Giroux said. "Coming into this game, we were the underdog. Everyone says we only play Hartford teams – that's what we always get – so we came here on the long bus ride, being the underdog, being down first and just coming back with everything we had and it just shows how hard we've worked this entire season and it's an unreal feeling."

The third-seeded Guardians, who are undefeated at 22-0, will face top-seeded St. Joseph, a perennial state power which last won a title in 2023, either Saturday or Sunday at a time to be determined at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford. St. Joseph beat Notre Dame-Fairfield in the other semifinal 1-0 in an overtime game that went to penalty kicks (5-3).

Glastonbury has come a long way from last season, when the Guardians went 8-5-3 and lost in the first round of the state tournament, and had to overcome some setbacks in the first half. Ridgefield, the No. 2 seed, scored early, less than two minutes into the game, on a goal by Ariana Gmelin. Then Glastonbury had a goal by Brenna Gregorski called back with 23 minutes left in the half because the ball wasn't stopped on the restart before the goal.

"I think honestly that kind of motivated us more because we got the goal so it showed we were in the game," Giroux said. "It gave us more momentum. We came out with more intensity."

And not long after that, Nikki Grant's goal tied the score for the Guardians.

"When we got the goal to tie the game up, it kind of gave us a little bit of energy toward the end of the first half," Landers said. "It gave us a little more belief we could get this done.

"Ridgefield is just an outstanding team – these are the kinds of games you're going to get when you get to this level. Game could have gone either way. They played great."

Ten minutes into the second half, freshman Teagan Gregorski scored what would be the game-winner. And then Glastonbury had to hang on, with the defense and sophomore goalkeeper Charlotte Mascheck keeping the Tigers, who pressed at the end, at bay.

"I'm not going to lie, it was really scary," Mascheck said. "But I have more confidence in my team than I do in myself.

"We worked our butts off to get to this point and it's really paying off."

#2728. Brian Schottenheimer: Christian Parker still has a bright future with the Cowboys

Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Mike Pettine will take over as the Cowboys’ defensive play-caller on Sunday. He replaces defensive coordinator Christian Parker, who will retain his title.

“Christian Parker is a huge part of what we’re trying to build here and that he is our defensive coordinator,” Schottenheimer said Wednesday, via Todd Archer of ESPN. “He is our leader. Parker, 34, arrived in January as a first-time play caller, leaving Philadelphia after two seasons as the Eagles’ defensive passing game coordinator. The Cowboys, though, rank last in yards (393.8), last in run defense (154.1) and last in third-down defense (48.8 percent). They are 30th in scoring (28.2).

Pettine arrived before Week 5 as a senior defensive assistant to help Parker, whom he brought into the NFL with the Packers in 2019. He was defensive coordinator with the Jets, when Schottenheimer was on staff, and also served in that role with the Bills and Packers.

Pettine was head coach of the Browns from 2014-15.

“When I look at this situation, we’re all committed to trying to get it right,” Schottenheimer said, “and so we’re making adjustments like we’ve made. We’ve made adjustments. We’ve adjusted some scheme. We’ve adjusted some personnel. We’ve adjusted some play time. This is just another adjustment where we’re trying to get right.”

Schottenheimer made clear several times that he still believes in Parker and still believes Parker has a future with the Cowboys.

“CP has a very, very bright future as a coach, but more specifically, a very bright future here as our defense coordinator,” Schottenheimer said.

#2725. Werder Bremen: The pressure of a European push

Once again, Werder Bremen supporters are dreaming of European football.

That wasn't expected to be the case going into this season. The prior campaign was an utter disaster, with the club barely avoiding relegation. They had to make a coaching change to save their skin, and even the new boss didn't really impress down the final stretch.

Bremen already had questions surrounding the squad, and things got even murkier when key names like Romano Schmid, Kerim Coulibaly, and Mio Backhaus were all sold. Replacements came in, sure, but no one knew if they'd be close to as good as the former players. There were also still major concerns in the attack.

All this happened, and then star man Jens Stage picked up an injury right before opening day that ruled him out for over four months. Then Werder were blown out on that first matchday away to Freiburg.

Despite everything, the team is now in the thick of the European push.

Bremen went into the international break in 6th, three points behind 4th place and three points ahead of 8th place. How in the world did that happen?

Well, midfield additions Yuri Reeger and Ludovit Reis hit the ground running, immediately playing at a top-tier level to cover for Stage and an injury-hit Senne Lynen. Mitchell Wieser completed his comeback to the team and brought a crucial spark to the pitch, scoring a remarkable stoppage-time winner vs Mainz. Karl Hein has impressed as the new number one, while Amos Pieper and Marco Friedl continued to shine at the back.

The attacking woes that were solved primarily by one man, the returning cult hero Niclas Fullkrug.

He scored in the opening round of the DFB Pokal via the spot, and then after a quiet week, he absolutely exploded. The German scored in eight straight contests, grabbing a total of 11 goals in that span. They were important goals too, either giving Bremen results or securing them on the day.

His addition has made others much better too. Marco Grull is a completely different player compared to last year, with 11 goal contributions to his name already. Another attacking loanee, Eren Dincki, has starred in moments.

This has all led to Werder's wonderful start. While supporters are thrilled with things so far, there's a newfound pressure on the club. They have to capitalize on this, and finally return to Europe.

Werder Bremen have not been involved in continental competition since 2010. That was a borderline disastrous Champions League campaign, where they finished 4th place in the old-school groups of four.

A return to the international stage would be a huge boost for a few reasons.

Most importantly, Bremen supporters have been without the marquee games for way too long. There's a certain aura to a European tie, whether it's a group stage matchup or a knockout round fixture. The chance to host a world power from another league, like La Liga, Serie A, or the Premier League, is what some dream of. The opportunity to then beat them is even bigger.

Even competitions like the Conference League have quality teams in them, and those are much easier to win. Werder certainly have enough talent to make a run in that competition or even the Europa League, especially after the format changes made recently. Those games are a huge bonus on top of the usual Bundesliga campaign.

The club itself could greatly benefit, too. The Green-Whites are far from the richest outfit on the planet, and they've been dancing around financial scares for the past few years. They've been forced to sell key talents, and even that hasn't been enough at times.

European competition means an additional revenue stream, and a big one at that. That is simply for qualifying and getting to play those opening league phase contests. Then, if you manage to go on a run, the prize money only increases the more you win. For Bremen, those funds would be absolutely crucial.

That money would not only fund new signings, but the mere fact of playing in Europe will make recruitment so much easier. Werder have had to look for hidden gems in the market, which sometimes works, but sometimes blows up in their face. Being able to add proven and ready-made talent to an already promising squad could keep them in the upper echelons of the league table.

You can't make Europe next season without winning games this season, and Bremen have two massive contests ahead of them in terms of this race.

They aren't playing any of the league's toughest teams, instead a bit of the opposite. First comes derby day, where Werder host bitter rivals Hamburg. While their Northern neighbors have picked up wins as of late, this is exactly the sort of opposition you have to beat to stay up the table. Add the hatred between the two, and you have a must-win meeting.

The Green-Whites get very lucky with the fact that they get to stay at home. They welcome Borussia Mönchengladbach, who currently sit in last place in the Bundesliga. It's clear to everyone why that's a game you simply have to earn all three points. If the hosts don't take the fixture seriously, though, then they'll set themselves up for a massive disappointment.

If Bremen play at their best, they'll be confident that six points will follow. That would keep them right at the top of the European picture, especially if they are lucky with results elsewhere. However, a false start or two could see them fall behind, where they'll never make their way back.

It might be the middle of November, but this stretch for Werder could go a long way in deciding on how their May turns out.

#2723. Berkshire breaks out to record high with fourth-quarter rally reaching 19%

(This is the Warren Buffett Watch newsletter, news and analysis on all things Warren Buffett and Berkshire Hathaway. You can sign up here to receive it every Friday evening in your inbox.)

Berkshire Hathaway's red-hot shares are ending a strong week with four consecutive fresh record high closes.

Since the rally began with the start of the fourth quarter on October 1, the Class A shares have closed at record highs 11 times as they soared 19.1%.

The much more widely held B shares closed at new highs just 10 times but are also up 19.1% from their near-term low.

The gains are in sharp contrast to the S&P 500's 1.2% dip as investors appear to be seeing Berkshire as a relatively safe haven amid worries about AI stocks and spending.

Both Berkshire classes were up 3.9% on the week as the S&P advanced by 2.5%, its best week since early August.

Berkshire's B shares are now 7.5 percentage points ahead of the benchmark for the year so far.

After erasing their post-Buffett CEO announcement losses three weeks ago, Berkshire shares are now up almost 10% since last year's shareholders meeting.

They've gained around 29% since last August's lows and are up around 18% year-to-date.

Berkshire Hathaway is due to disclose its quarterly equity portfolio snapshot on Monday when it files its Q3 13F with the SEC.

We won't know for sure until then, but numbers in the company's third quarter 10-Q, released last Saturday, indicate Berkshire continued to reduce its Bank of America stake.

It would be the ninth consecutive quarter of selling.

As of June 30, Berkshire reported holding 483.4 million BAC shares valued now at $24.7 billion, it's fifth largest equity position.

On June 30, 2024, before the selling began, Berkshire owned just over 1 billion shares valued at $41.1 billion.

Since then, the number of shares in the portfolio has decreased by 53.2%, not including any Q3 sales, while the stock price has increased by 28.3%.

If there had been no reductions, the position would be worth $52.7 billion.

The belief Berkshire sold more BAC shares in the third quarter is based on a $372 million reduction in the cost basis for equities categorized by the company as "banks, insurance, and finance."

The 10-Q also reports $2.2 billion of pretax gains from equity sales.

Barron's notes Bank of America and American Express are the only financial stocks in the portfolio that have a cost basis low enough to generate a gain like that. Amex is one of the four stocks new CEO Greg Abel indicated would be held for "decades" to come in his February letter to shareholders.

In any case, Berkshire's almost 23% stake in Amex would have required it to quickly disclose any sales.

Based on the numbers in the 10-Q, the warrants Berkshire received as part of a 2011 $5 billion investment in the bank that it used in 2017 to buy 700 million shares at $7.14 each, and BAC's average stock price in the quarter, Barron's estimates 30 to 40 million shares may have been sold.

That would be roughly in line with the 30.2 million shares sold in the second quarter.

The case isn't as good, but Barron's thinks Berkshire may have bought more Alphabet shares in the period. That's based on a $2.3 billion increase in the cost basis for the category that includes Google's parent.

Overall, it looks like it will be a relatively quiet quarter with $2.4 billion in equity purchases and $2.8 billion in sales.

In the first quarter, Berkshire bought $15.9 billion and sold $24.1 billion of equities. In the second quarter, it purchased $23.5 billion and sold $3.7 billion.

All those numbers exclude the company's buybacks of its own stock.

In a term sheet filed early Friday, Berkshire Hathaway says it is selling more than 182 billion yen ($1.1 billion) worth of bonds with maturities between 2029 and 2056 and annual interest rates between 2.6% and 4.6%.

Bloomberg points out the rates, compared to benchmarks, are higher than its previous sale this year.

It quotes a fund manager as saying market sentiment "has become more sensitive," forcing issuers to make their offerings more attractive.

In April, Berkshire sold 272 billion yen ($1.7 billion) of bonds.

Berkshire uses the proceeds from the yen-denominated bonds to protect its ongoing investments in Japanese stocks from currency fluctuations.

Warren Buffett recommends Benjamin Graham's book, "The Intelligent Investor," and outlines what he considers Graham's three most important ideas.

WARREN BUFFETT: On investment books, if you're asking about that, I would recommend the first two books that Phil Fisher wrote back around 1960, "Common Sense [Stocks] and Uncommon Profits" and the second one ["Paths to Wealth Through Common Stocks"]. They're very good books.

You know, I obviously recommend, first and foremost, [Benjamin Graham's] "The Intelligent Investor," with chapters eight and 20 are the ones that you really should read.

Two of the — well, all of the important ideas in investing, really, are in that book, because there's only about three ideas. And those — two of them are emphasized in those two chapters...

One is that — to think of yourself — to think of investing as owning a business and not buying something that wiggles around in price.

And the second one is your attitude, which ties in with that, the attitude toward the market, that's covered in chapter eight. And if you have the proper attitude toward market movements, it's an enormous help in securities.

And the final chapter is on the margin of safety, which means, don't try and drive a 9,800-pound truck over a bridge that says it's, you know, "Capacity: 10,000 pounds." But go down the road a little bit and find one that says, "Capacity: 15,000 pounds."

The Cleveland Cavaliers fell to the Memphis Grizzlies 124-121. Sam Merrill had an opportunity to tie or take the lead with a pair of free throws in the final seconds, and missed them both.

It was a high-scoring first quarter despite neither team shooting the ball well from behind the three-point line. Both the Cavs and Grizzlies shot below 30% from downtown in the opening quarter, but scored over 30 points each.

Donovan Mitchell led the way in the first quarter with 10 points on 5-for-8 shooting (5-of-6 inside two-point range). He's done a great job of getting downhill and applying pressure on the rim this week, such as in his 39-point performance over the Chicago Bulls on Monday.

Mitchell finished with 34 points tonight on 14-for-27 shooting.

The score was 72-71 at halftime. Taylor Hendricks, Cam Spencer and Cedric Coward combined for 31 points on a perfect 10-for-10 shooting in the first half. It was an offense-first type of game.

Points in the paint were key. Each team scored 34 points in the paint during the first half, with the Cavs shooting 17-for-21 from that zone and the Grizzlies converting on 17-of-19 attempts. Those aggressive attacks on the basket also led to 33 free throws between both teams in the first two quarters. So, even though it was a high-scoring game, it wasn't exactly high-octane.

The Cavs were without Evan Mobley, Peyton Watson, and Jaylon Tyson tonight.

The Grizzlies did not have Ty Jerome, who missed tonight's game with a right hip impingement.

Rookie Meleek Thomas contributed 14 points on 4-of-6 three-point shooting. His on-ball juice off the bench has helped Cleveland survive this stretch of injuries.

Mario Hezonja filled in for his first start of the season, posting 16 points, 7 rebounds and 5 assists on 7-for-12 shooting. Hezonja's been a nice pickup for the Cavs this season and has made it past the point where his contract becomes guaranteed this season — meaning Mario is here to stay.

Norchad Omier had another strong night on the glass, grabbing three offensive rebounds in the same possession as he continues to work his way into Kenny Atkinson's rotation.

The Cavs ultimately weren't able to get stops when they needed them. It was too easy in the paint for Memphis throughout the night, and that resulted in a loss for Cleveland.

#2720. Pundit thinks confidence makes or breaks Florian Wirtz

Florian Wirtz has plenty of admirers (and some haters, too).

However, former Chelsea defender Frank Sinclair is not fully convinced that comparisons between the Liverpool midfielder and former Napoli, Parma, and Napoli star Gianfranco Zola are particularly accurate.

Who even knew these comparisons were going on? Well, apparently they are, so let's explore.

Sinclair believes the two players are completely different, while also pointing to the increasingly difficult environment modern number tens face in today's game.

Speaking to online casino site Betano about the comparisons, Sinclair made his position abundantly clear, insisting that Zola was in a category of his own and explaining why Wirtz faces a different set of challenges.

"Similarities between Florian Wirtz and Gianfranco Zola? No, none whatsoever. I'm sorry to say, but you cannot put Wirtz in the same category as Gianfranco Zola. I think Gianfranco settled into the Premier League straight away. He was an instant success and an incredible player, I've openly said the best player I ever played with and probably one of the best players ever to play for Chelsea, which Chelsea supporters have voted for before," Sinclair said. "I don't really see the comparison. I don't feel they play the same way. I think Zola was very much a second center-forward that had freedom to go all over the pitch and affect the game from wherever he felt he could do. I feel like Wirtz is more of definitely a number ten that plays in that pocket and that area. But it's really difficult for number tens in this day and age because teams are set up not to give them that much space and time on the ball.

"I see why he has the issues that he has. You think about number tens now, how many number tens are really dominating games? It takes Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer both to be in great form to be a real threat, and they both play in the pockets in the wider areas. So for one person to be playing in that ten role, it's a really difficult task now to really affect games. But obviously, he's a player that looks like he's built on confidence, and when his confidence is high, then he looks like a real handful and can affect games. But I certainly don't see the comparison with Gianfranco Zola."

Sinclair's comments offer an interesting perspective on Wirtz's adaptation to English football. Rather than simply questioning the German international's ability, he highlights the tactical difficulties associated with operating as a traditional number ten in a Premier League increasingly designed to suffocate creative players in central areas.

That does not necessarily make Wirtz any less talented, but it does underline why finding the right role, building confidence, and getting consistent opportunities to influence games will be so important for his development at Liverpool — even if he never becomes a reasonable facsimile of Zola.

#2718. With no Maxey, Brown, Sixers overcome putrid start to earn gritty win

The Sixers overcame their leading scorer being scratched late and a 17-point deficit to defeat the Orlando Magic 121-116 Wednesday night.

Joel Embiid led the Sixers with 26 points along with six rebounds and seven assists, shooting 7-of-18 from the floor. LeBron James went for 22 points, three rebounds and six assists on 8-of-18 shooting.

VJ Edgecombe excelled with a bigger workload, finishing with a season-high 24 points, going 8-of-15 from the floor, along with eight rebounds and six assists. Franz Wagner led all scorers with 27.

Tyrese Maxey was ruled out right before gametime with soreness in his right foot. Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade were both out for the Sixers with hamstring strains, along with Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow. Paolo Banchero, Jonathan Isaac and Noah Penda were out for Orlando.

Orlando's first six shots of the game were from behind the arc, and they made three of them before making their first three two-pointers of the night. LeBron opened the game by burying a three and set up Embiid for an easy layup. Edgecombe was able to get to the line trying to create a fast break, but threw a bad pass that turned into a turnover a few moments later.

Not only did the Sixers go nearly five minutes without a field goal after that Embiid layup, but the big fella came up limping a bit after getting fouled by Wendell Carter Jr.. He also bumped into Goga Bitadze on the play, but didn't leave the game.

The Sixers were also not giving Orlando any type of resistance. The Magic made 11 of their first 14 field goals of the game. They haven't looked this bad in healthier lineups, but the Magic seemed pretty happy to pick on combo of Anfernee Simons and Labaron Philon Jr. on the perimeter.

On the other end, Philon did make his first three shots of the night and ran down a pass that nearly sailed out of bounds to save a fast break. They didn't come up with any answers for a Magic team that shot 69% from the field in the first quarter, getting out to a 13-point lead over Philly.

Tacko Fall did check into the game late into the first for a near six-minute shift. It feels like the Sixers almost have to sit in a zone when he's out there. So far, he's presented a challenging and different enough look to alter shots near him, he also caught a lob from LeBron. His mobility really doesn't help the team's defensive rebounding, but being able to swat a shot was the most resistance the defense had to that point.

Nick Nurse continued to try out his two-way guys, subbing in Caleb Love early in the second. His first shot of the night was a three that bounced off the rim and backboard before falling in. It took a bit to fall, but it helped the Sixers climb back as LeBron had begun to carry the offense forward.

The Magic had successfully squashed the momentum of a 9-0 Sixers run, then Desmond Bane decided to grab Embiid's crotch for some reason as he fought through Embiid's screen. Despite a review, the play was still deemed a common foul.

There was another scary moment where LeBron appeared to slip on a wet spot on the floor and immediately came up favoring his groin area. The Sixers immediately called timeout, but James remained in the game.

After that timeout Embiid started to shake off his slow start to the night. He worked a two-man game to get Simons a three before going to work himself in the post. He cleaned up his own miss and drew a foul in the process, then filled the paint to give Edgecombe an easy assist. He picked up two blocks on the other end, one of which had to be overturned by a challenge. They capitalized on the stop as Edgecombe drilled another pull-up at the buzzer to pull the Sixers within five at the break.

Thanks to LeBron turning the ball over and getting his shot blocked, the Magic easily pushed their lead back up to double digits. The Sixers called a quick timeout, mostly to give Edgecombe a breather after getting hit in the eye. The stoppage worked to their favor as they picked up a couple buckets and forced a turnover coming out of the timeout.

Wagner was able to exploit some weak points, especially as they continued to sit in a zone, but every Sixer on the floor had dramatically turned around their defensive effort. They've looked pretty good at scrambling and rotating over to help, which is impressive given how many new parts there are.

After going scoreless in Brooklyn, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope had a much easier time finding the basket, making three of his first four shots on the night. Embiid knocked down a fadeaway jumper and drew a foul on a drive to help the Sixers keep slowly crawling back.

All quarter the Sixers were able to get within a basket, but weren't able to put together a stop and a score that would give themselves the lead. They only had given up seven offensive rebounds, but that turned into 18 second-chance points for the Magic. The Sixers got three chances of their own to close the quarter, but Embiid got swung a grenade he couldn't get off in time, leaving the Sixers still down five after the third.

Justin Edwards also got his first real minutes of the year. He made a nice hustle play or two in the first half, but has just been in a terrible shooting slump going back to the preseason. He had a really bad airball as the Sixers started another quarter slow offensively. Edgecombe drilled a couple threes to keep the offense afloat, and thanks to more solid Tacko Fall minutes, the Sixers didn't lose any ground.

Even with his four turnovers, Edgecombe scaled up very well. The shot he likes to go to is that midrange pull-up off a pick-and-roll and he was in a groove from there tonight. After making another, Embiid got to the line to tie the game for the first time since the beginning of the game. Using an Embiid screen, Edgecombe got downhill to get Jabari Walker wide open for three. Walker drilled it to give the Sixers their first lead since those opening minutes, and force a Magic timeout with five minutes to go.

That timeout allowed LeBron to check back into the game, and he powered his way for a layup to keep the Sixers up by two shortly after. Embiid followed that up by swatting away Anthony Black's heave to beat the buzzer. Black fouled Embiid as he came down with the rebound, putting him at the line and the Sixers in the bonus.

After Embiid drilled both free throws, Wagner got to the basket then found Jalen Suggs on the wing to put the Magic back in front with two minutes to go. Edgecombe responded with a grenade to put the Sixers back in front, then tapped a long rebound off of Bane to come up with a big stop on the other end.

LeBron drilled a pull-up to extend that lead, but ended up fouling Suggs on the other end. Suggs split the pair though, and James found Simons in the corner for a three that sealed the game. Simons finished with 18 points in his spot-start, drilling the dagger in front of his friends and family.

#2713. Nets put up a dud vs the Bulls, lose 137-107

It wasn't just a fitting, but a necessary night for the Brooklyn Nets to celebrate their ABA roots. The present looks bleak, and the future murky at best. At this point, it feels like we have no choice but to seek refuge in the past.

Prior to tonight's game, Brooklyn hosted a panel featuring hoop legends Julius Erving and Brian Taylor, who spoke on the franchise's first two ABA Championships in 1974 and 1976. They also gave out ABA-inspired merch, hosted a dunk show at halftime, and payed homage to each championship team's other players in a variety of ways.

I have no memory of the ABA, so the nostalgia didn't appeal to me, but that made the whole ordeal even more impressive from my point of view. The organization used every opportunity it had to celebrate this group of men, who's legacies could've easily been washed away as the team changed leagues, cities, and names over the years. In their smiles and body language, you could tell it meant a lot to them, and that was pretty damn cool.

They weren't the only Nets of yore in the house. For the first time in his seven year career, Nic Claxton played in the Barclays Center as a visitor this evening. A member of the Chicago Bulls since Brooklyn shipped him out over the summer in a three-team deal to bring in Julius Randle, Clax was happy to be back, and spoke positively about the organization at shootaround a few hours before tipoff.

"I got the fam here. I feel like I also got fam that's here working for the Nets, so you know, it'll be good," he said. "No ill will at all. It's all good vibes. I don't have nothing negative to say about anybody in this organization in Brooklyn. I'm grateful for my time here. I had a beautiful time here. Cultivated a lot of great relationships, so it's all love."

Usually, nobody likes getting traded or cut. But after an abundance of rocky, or at best ominous exits from presumed franchise cornerstones over the past few years, that's refreshing to hear.

Brooklyn's on-court product tonight was anything but. In wasn't just stale, but rotten, and the kind of thing that makes you question every decision made since committing to a rebuild. Julius Randle called it one of the worst games he's ever been a part of.

Both teams, sitting in the Eastern Conference's basement with 3-10 records, looked the part early on. They combined for five turnovers in the game's first three minutes. Chicago got six points off theirs while Brooklyn got just a deuce, so the Bulls began the game up 12-6.

Brooklyn's defense was equally uninspiring. Chicago benefitted form an abundance of open looks as Egor Dëmin consistency got beat off the dribble the top of the key, leading to easy drive-and-kick actions. The Nets also allowed seven offensive rebounds in the first, leading to 18 second chance points.

So, the Bulls led by even more at the end of the period, up by a 37-21 score. And then five minutes later, they were up 55-32. Brooklyn stopped giving up every other rebound in their own end, but kept defending poorly on perimeter, allowing the Chicago to open the period 4-5 from downtown. They ended up going 15-29 in the first half, hitting a franchise record. Coming into the game tonight, no NBA shot worse from three than the Bulls.

"Everything was uncontested, and it's happened before," Fernández said. "We've addressed it. I think that I remember the Boston game. We had the effort to go and contest shots and so forth. And sometimes I don't know, like we forget, and we have to be reminded again."

Nine of those threes came from the corner, where Brooklyn has been especially vulnerable so far this year. Only the Los Angeles Clippers and Sacramento Kings are allowing their opponents to shoot a higher clip form there this year. Postgame, Randle said it all starts on the interior, however.

"Not sure, not sure," he said. "But I mean, they were living in our painting at will tonight, getting into the paint and spraying the basketball. So I'm not sure exactly why the corner three was open, but I felt like we didn't stop them at all in the paint tonight."

Brooklyn trailed at the break 76-51. Among Brooklyn's prospects, Nolan Traoré was once again a candle on dark, desolate night. He had 11 points at half and two dimes while shooting 5-8 from the field. Outside of he and Julius Randle, all other Nets combined to shoot 9-23 from the field.

It was Brooklyn's third straight game going into the half down more than 20 points. When asked about instructing his team to start better, Fernández made it clear his message hasn't been getting through.

"I can try to say it in Spanish, because in English they don't understand," he said. "So, I'll keep trying and find whatever language works, but yeah, effort was not good."

At the break, when the Nets brought out all their ABA champs, Erving shared a few words, and at the end of his speech, he encouraged the Nets to make comeback.

Dëmin seemed to take it upon himself to reduce the deficit in the third, putting up 11 of the team's first 14 shots in the period, which drew mixed results. Either attacking off screens or occasionally catching flat footed defenders in transition, he got the rim four times and finished on three of them. He was equally aggressive, but far less accurate from deep though, going 1-6 from downtown in the frame.

"Within the game, I saw opportunities, and I took them," Dëmin said.

The Nets were still down 30+ once the bench group checked in, and Chicago's reserves proceeded to outscore Brooklyn's 20-9 in the third. As that period trickled into the fourth, the effort went from poor to nonexistent, as the Nets also gave up another 10 second chance points and got outscored 24-14 on the interior.

"We were not a competitive group," Fernández said. "We were not a connected group. We were not a selfless group. So I saw selfishness. I saw pointing fingers, and you know, and I saw guys that didn't always play hard."

The fourth quarter, or the open-to-public scrimmage vs Chicago, saw Brown Jr. put in 12 points and drop two assists while shooting 3-4 from the field and 2-3 from deep. He finished with an 15/4/1 line.

"It's 82 games," Brown said. "We have to mark it off and move on from it, but obviously learn from it as well. We'll watch film to tomorrow, see some things that we have to fix, but I mean, you can't each effort. You know everybody says that."

If you were to have anyone put lipstick on a pig with a strong performance in garbage time, your top pick is probably the best choice. But in terms of positives, that's about it, and frankly feels like charitable thing to mention anyway. The defense never found its way, and after eight minutes of run in the second half, playing Porter Jr. and Randle wasn't worth it anymore. MPJ. finished with just five points while shooting 1-7 from the field. Randle finished with 17 points on 5-10 shooting.

"That was embarrassing," Randle said. "Been in the league for 13 years, and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. Like, you lose by 30 sometimes. It's just a bad night, but it's how we did it. That just wasn't cool."

The Nets will host the Orlando Magic on Friday, who've won four of their last five, but will need to face themselves first as well. I don't expect either to be easy.

"I think when you win, you find ways to win. When you lose, you find excuses. Seems like a lot of excuses," Randle said. "So, you know, for me, I got to go back into work. I got to go back into the film. I got to figure out how to look myself in the mirror tonight too, like everybody else, and figure out what I can do better. Not point the finger or anything. Like I got to figure out as a man, you know, pride that has played this game since a kid and love it, and has given a lot to me, I got to figure out how I can help the team and be better for the team. So, you know, I put it on me."

Final: Chicago Bulls 137, Brooklyn Nets 107

The Nets will host the Orlando Magic before getting back on the road on Friday evening. At the time of writing, Orlando has won four straight after beginning their season 2-7 with Franz Wagner playing at an All-Star pace. It'll be his first time NBA game with his brother, Mo, as an adversary rather than a teammate. Hopefully the brotherly love prevails and he takes it easy on all of us. This one tips off at 7:30 p.m. EST.

#2710. Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo sniffs triple-double in first game vs. Bucks; Tyler Herro booed while Bam Adebayo stars in win

More than four months after the news broke that Miami Heat big man Bam Adebayo punched Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro, Adebayo delivered another blow against Herro — this one in the form of a vindicating 21 first-half points in their first game between one another.

During a Wednesday night showdown rich with storylines, Adebayo at one point scored nine in a row and connected on a trio of 3-pointers over the opening two quarters.

Of course, all the while, Giannis Antetokounmpo was facing the team he was synonymous with for 13 seasons. And the matchup was taking place in Miami's Kaseya Center, which doubled as "Vice City" on the eve of the highly anticipated nationwide release of Grand Theft Auto VI.

Antetokounmpo played the facilitator role with nine assists and still managed 27 points in the Heat's 137-130 victory over the Bucks. Adebayo finished with 26 points. Herro, meanwhile, was booed throughout and clocked out with just eight points on 4-of-11 shooting.

Miami (9-6) has now won six consecutive games after a 3-6 start. Milwaukee (1-14), on the other hand, remains dead last in the East.

Herro is a Milwaukee native, but Miami is where he began his NBA career. In that way, Wednesday was a homecoming for him. The same could be said for Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakučionis, who also started their NBA journeys with the Heat before being shipped off to the Bucks in the Antetokounmpo trade.

The blockbuster deal also delivered the Bucks the 13th overall pick in this year's draft — which they used to select Tennessee forward Nate Ament — as well as future draft considerations, including two more first-round picks.

In addition to Antetokounmpo, the Heat received Bobby Portis, who became a fan favorite in Milwaukee while helping the "Greek Freak" lead the franchise to its first NBA championship in 50 years back in 2021.

The end of Antetokounmpo's tenure with the Bucks was dominated by drama, particularly as the two-time league MVP and 10-time All-Star feuded with the organization over his health.

Miami gave him a fresh start, and the Antetokounmpo-piloted Heat are taking off under longtime head coach Erik Spoelstra.

Herro's Bucks are on the other end of the NBA spectrum, clearly entrenched in a Taylor Jenkins-directed rebuild. Herro heard the jeers of Miami fans over the course of the night.

Even though he won NBA Sixth Man of the Year during the 2021-22 campaign and earned All-Star recognition with the Heat in the 2024-25 season, his reputation in Miami took a hit this offseason.

Critical commentary Herro shared about Adebayo on social media led to the infamous physical altercation between the former teammates in Las Vegas ahead of Summer League action. They shared the floor together in Miami from 2019-26. In that span, the Heat made a pair of NBA Finals appearances.

But there was ostensibly no love lost by the end of that seven-season stretch. As reported in July by the Miami Herald, around that time, Herro posted a graphic on Instagram that listed the league's worst midrange shooters last season. Antetokounmpo topped that unfortunate leaderboard at 26.8%, and Adebayo came in 10th at 35.9%, per the Herald.

Plus, screenshots circulated of a direct message conversation, in which comments seemingly questioning Adebayo's play and contract were attributed to Herro online.

Herro said shortly after the dustup that he wanted to "move on" from the incident, except it was top of mind for everyone watching Wednesday's game.

Adebayo said afterward that he didn't get to talk to Herro but that he's not someone who holds grudges. He noted that he's "on to the next thing."

"I feel like I got great karma," Adebayo added, via Will Manso of WPLG Local 10 News.

Adebayo's nine straight points arrived in the second quarter. He capped that surge by stepping in front of a pass from Jaquez and turning the steal into a two-handed flush that staked Miami to a 48-28 advantage.

The Heat were in control from the jump. They went 22 of 48 from 3, including 13 of 28 in the first half. Klay Thompson continued his hot streak with four triples and 13 points.

Antetokounmpo orchestrated several of the team's 3-pointers. His dribble-drive penetration set the stage for kickouts, most notably a no-look dish that rewarded Adebayo early on.

Antetokounmpo's first points didn't come until the 5:11 mark of the first quarter. His first field goal gave the Heat their 70th point. In the process, though, he had an effect that extended far beyond his scoring.

Maybe his most impressive moment was when he rose up to deny Bucks rookie guard Brayden Burries with a two-handed rejection at the rim late in the second quarter.

In the third quarter, Antetokounmpo swung a shrewd shovel pass to Andrew Wiggins, who promptly cashed in from long range.

Then Antetokounmpo slammed home a lob from Adebayo, showing off what they can do in the two-man game.

Antetokounmpo stacked 14 rebounds and ended up an assist shy of a triple-double. He told reporters postgame that he didn't think it felt weird facing Milwaukee.

"Look, I think since I was a kid, when I play basketball, I try to lock in as much as I can," Antetokounmpo said, per The Athletic's Eric Nehm. "People that have been around me know how I operate on game days. I try not to say much. I try not to interact as much. And the only thing on my mind is, 'How can I help my team win and how can I do my job?' It doesn't matter who I play.

"… I could have been playing against my four brothers and my two sons. It doesn't matter. I try to do my best and try to do the things that I've worked on and try to have fun. It doesn't matter what uniform I go against."

His old team made made things look closer than they actually were down the stretch. The Bucks were paced by Kyle Kuzma (26 points), Burries (20) and Jakučionis (20).

Milwaukee is a ways from competing for a playoff spot again, whereas Miami is shaping up to be a threat in the Eastern Conference, just like the Bucks were all those years with Antetokounmpo.

The franchises are linked because of this summer's trade and what happened in its aftermath.

And on Wednesday, the Heat led by as many as 30 points, as Antetokounmpo and Adebayo flexed their value.

Talent will be added, there will come a time when suddenly we are that better team and should win !

Phoenix6 cares about kickers even if you don't!

Cutie0716 is happy with how the team is being built from the ground up.

I looked at the roster and counted 15 rookies on the 53. Not including the ones on the Injured list and the PS.

These rookies are playing the way I had wished our rookies of yesterday would have played. Let them play. Let them make mistakes. These guys are really developing a nucleus. I HONESTLY don't care about wins and losses.

Every game I read about, I read how tough the D is getting. How they are fighting until the end. These guys are hungry. This is going to be a big deal with our 2027 draft picks.

It's one thing to be on a losing team, but when MORE THAN HALF of the whole team are rookies, it makes a statement. They are playing hard and meaningfully. I give the Coach and GM credit for picking their own guys.

Proctor will be, if he's not already there, a beast by next year. A rookie that our team depended on. It's wonderful. No one thought that Proctor would be our pick.

I knew months ago that we wouldn't win much. Some were predicting five wins. If we win 2-3, BUT ESTABLISHING building blocks, we have done a great job.

The building of a cohesive team is all that we need right now. I know that most of you, if not all, strongly disagree with my opinion, and that's fine. You have your own opinion. No problem. I gave you mine. I love to see the replays on NFLN because I see HOW HARD these guys play. I CHEER THEM FOR THAT. And so should you.

StanleyDoyle1 is happy with the rookies' contributions so far.

My takeway: I cannot remember a season when more rookies had a meaningful impact on the team. This season, Rodriguez, Proctor, Johnson, Douglas, Taafe have all shown real talent and made a meaningful difference in games. Kacmarek, Bell and Coleman have shown promise. That's eight rookies. 2020 had 7 contributors. 2012 had 6. 2007 had 5. 1997 had 6. To find something comparable to this season, you have to go back to 1982 when they had 12 rounds to find as many contributors from the draft.

Luvs2drnk took a different stance from StanleyDoyle1.

If we were winning more games, I'd be inclined to agree with you. But the main reason we have so many rookies playing meaningful snaps is due to the gutting of the roster. So while they are getting meaningful snaps on our team, not so sure they would do the same on a competitive team. I'd give you Rod, Proc, Johnson, and Douglas although the first 3 would be the only ones who would likely be starting on any other team. Taafe has shown some potential, need to see more consistancy. Kac likely becomes a blocking TE with little to no impact as a receiving TE, which is disappointing for a 3rd rounder. Bell could still develop, but won't likely have any impact till next year hopefully. Coleman could eventually replace Washington or fade into obscurity if more talented receiving options are added. The fact we got 4-5 potential long term starters out of this class is a feat in itself, and that definitely bodes well for next year's draft. Let's just hope they have better luck in the FA department next year. I'll give this year a pass due to cap restrictions.

Well, it was a bit slow, but I guess the fans' overall enthusiasm is down because of the losing, and those fans choosing something else to do right now are missing out on seeing these rookies ball out. Anway, thank you to each of you who took the time to join in and answer our Phinsider Question Of The Day.

#2703. Pistons at Pelicans final score: No Cade, No Problem

With as long as Detroit's injury report has been recently, it got a little longer with Cade Cunningham as a late addition tonight. After the Pistons' big win against San Antonio last night, it's no surprise Deuce got some rest on the second night of a back-to-back.

JB Bickerstaff, with his shorthanded roster, rolled out the unusual starting lineup of Daniss Jenkins, Kevin Huerter, Javonte Green, Ausar Thompson, and John Collins. This would've been a great game for Ebuka Okorie to get some minutes, but he hurt his hip with the Motor City Cruise just the other day.

This meant Detroit's key bench pieces were Paul Reed, Chaz Lanier, and Elijah Harkless. Even Tolu Smith saw some spot minutes when Collins and Reed both needed rest. Luckily, Isaiah Joe made his return to the lineup tonight after missing the last several games. Despite having to play guys from the end of the bench and on two-way spots, Detroit didn't struggle against New Orleans.

Remember that unusual starting lineup for Detroit? Well, every single one of them finished in double digits. Jenkins, Green, and Collins all made at least three three-pointers. Jenkins, Thompson, and Huerter all had at least four assists, though Huerter had seven and DJ added nine.

Both Lanier and Joe made three three-pointers off the bench. Reed was the key sixth man once again, though that's not all that peculiar nowadays. Harkless played his most minutes so far this season and did a great job sharing the rock with four assists.

In a game without their star player, this was another complete team win. There's no doubt the depth on this team is one of the best in the league, and Detroit had seven different players score in double digits. Your Detroit Pistons are now 10-4 on the year.

#2701. UConn Men's Basketball: Huskies Fall to Arizona in Tough Road Test

Dan Hurley had to have known when he scheduled nonconference games against six ranked teams – plus Power Four school Ohio State – that his UConn Huskies would not emerge unscathed.

He gave up the early season "buy" games that could have padded the win total and replaced them with contests against the highest-quality opponents to prepare his team for March Madness and a quest for another national championship.

Hurley wanted tests, he wanted hostile road environments. No. 12 Arizona and a raucous home crowd in Tucson provided just that as the Wildcats led wire-to-wire to defeat the No. 3 Huskies 85-79 on Wednesday night.

Arizona also defeated UConn last season, 71-67, in Storrs, Conn., in the first game of a home-and-away series.

On Wednesday, Arizona came out of the locker room and controlled the tempo from the start, using a swarming defense to stifle the Huskies and get them off their game. The Wildcats took a 10-0 lead, expanded it to 19 and were up 47-29 at halftime.

That defense limited UConn to just 33.9% (23 of 68) shooting for the game.

Still, UConn outplayed Arizona in the second half and cut the lead to eight points five times, but the Wildcats had an answer eavh time before ending with a six-point triumph

Here's what we learned about the Huskies (4-1) in the loss to the Wildcats (4-1).

Well, on second thought, we already knew that.

But every game, he seems to rise to a new level. He scored a career-high 29 points in the face of defensive pressure – his fourth game this season with 20-plus points – and also showed off his defensive skills.

He played 36 minutes and showed he is capable of putting the team on his back when necessary.

Sophomore transfers Na'jai Hines and Oskar Giltay are young and still learning, and they got a good lesson on Wednesday.

They weren't really a match for 7-foot-2 Motiejus Krivas or 6-7 Ivan Kharchenkov, who isn't afraid to mix it up on the inside.

Arizona's Motiejus Krivas dunks the ball during the second half against UConn on Wednesday night. He scored 18 points. Aryanna Frank-Imagn Images

Krivas scored 18 points on 7-of-8 shooting and had 12 rebounds and four blocks. Kharchenkov delivered 20 points, five rebounds and seven assists. Three of his rebounds were on the offensive glass.

Perhaps it was fear of foul trouble, but in the first half, Hines and Giltay did not aggressively go after rebounds as they combined for four. Hines grabbed seven in the second half to wind up with nine as UConn outscored Arizona 50-38.

The centers will need to work on being aggressive without getting into foul trouble and hone those skills before the NCAA Tournament.

Landrew started his second game in place of the injured Nik Khamenia and showed fans why he was one of the top recruits in the nation in the 2026 class – a five-star and the No. 27 player overall, according to the 247Sports composite. After a quiet first half of zero points and one rebound in 17 minutes, Landrew finished with 12 points and a team-high 10 boards.

#2700. Player Grades: Cavs vs. Grizzlies – Cleveland loses back-and-forth affair

The Cleveland Cavaliers dropped Wednesday's offensive showdown 124-121 to the Memphis Grizzlies.

Grades are based on our usual expectations for each player.

34 points, 3 rebounds, 3 assists, 1 steal

Mitchell has been on a heater as of late.

It appears the momentum generated from Monday's matchup against the Chicago Bulls carried over as Mitchell was once again scoring at will. The Cavaliers found themselves in a constant back-and-forth, and Mitchell was the counterpunch Cleveland needed more times than not.

Nights like these are perfect responses for why the Cavaliers still can rely on Mitchell.

As of late, it feels like Harden is looking to be more of a distributor than a scorer. He was not hunting for scoring opportunities, and while it is nice to see Harden not force his way out of the slump, it is discouraging to see that this is the role he needs now.

Some might deem this as the right transition for Harden as he enters the late stage of his career. In terms of the Cavaliers' postseason outlook, it doesn't really make the roster that much better.

Allen had a tough task against the height of the Grizzlies. He was either matching up against Zach Edey or Cameron Boozer for stretches, and their height really put Allen to the test throughout the game.

It felt like at times that Allen was getting a lot of physicality and not being rewarded by the whistle. He responded to these challenges well, still finding ways to score despite not getting the calls. A great performance from Allen, where toughness was a key factor.

Proctor had his most forgettable performance in a minute against Memphis. Being named a starter again was deserved with the string of games that Proctor has put together. However, not every game is going to trend upwards; games like this will happen from time to time.

It was nice to see that even when Proctor is not firing away, he stays level-headed and does not become impatient with the lack of opportunities.

Finally, Mario has got the nod to be in the starting five. It only took injuries to nearly the entire Cavaliers roster, but we finally got there.

Hezonja continues to be a force when out on the floor. Whether it's his physicality or ability to knock down shots from the perimeter, Hezonja impresses me at every turn. Nights like these will only make the cries for his minutes to ramp up louder.

There is no one else on the Cavaliers roster who really can match the unique traits that Hezonja provides. At times, it feels like the opponents do not really have an idea of how to match him either.

Merrill looked like a man who was not out for the past few games. All he did was put his head down to get to the basket and fight for offensive boards.

While Merrill was not lighting up the scoreboard, he did show a lot of hustle and grit. While that will not please many, I was fine with this outing from a guy who was shelved for a bit.

Then, he missed two free throws that cost the Cavs the game.

Grade: C+ before free-throw misses, D+ after

14 points, 2 rebounds, 2 assists, 1 steal

Thomas is so consistent offensively. It is insane that the Cavaliers' second-round pick continues to contribute to the offense in such valuable stretches.

The shot is legit. Thomas's ability to shoot from almost anywhere, whether on the move or catch-and-shoot, allows him to fit very easily into any of the Cavaliers' five-man lineups.

Quality minutes from Bryant, however, with the lineups and athletic size of Memphis, it wasn't a great use of his skill set.

Omier is just a hustler. There is no second of this game where his effort will be questioned. On a team where it feels like there will be lapses, he will be a reliable hustler and a reminder of the effort needed to win games.
