#2699. NFL Week 11 Injury Report: Drake Maye likely done for season, surgery for Jordan Addison

Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in.

Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday.

**UPDATED AS OF WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 18 AT 8:15 PM ET**

Impact: Likely none, though the Bills will employ a run-heavy approach against the Dolphins.

Palmer managed only seven offensive snaps in Week 8 before departing with an aggravation of the hamstring injury he has battled since Week 4. He was placed on injured reserve.

Impact: Not much, honestly. Palmer has played sparingly this season in a situational role, although his absence could leave room for Skyler Bell to be active for the third time this season. The Bills also activated Tyrell Shavers (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list. He could join the wide receiver rotation but does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season.

Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright. The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season.

The Dolphins placed Willis on injured reserve in Week 10. He will be eligible to return in Week 14, but Willis is seeking a second opinion after the injury progressed into his abdomen. Season-ending surgery is possible, although the team has yet to decide if or when surgery would take place.

Impact: Kyle McCord's installation as the team's starter hurts all involved. Until we see how McCord fares in this system, only Ollie Gordon is a safe FLEX starter.

Bell is listed as doubtful for Week 10 against the Colts. He is day-to-day entering Week 11. Impact: Bell has largely been unable to get anything going during his rookie season, with the team leaning more heavily on Malik Washington and Caleb Douglas (shoulder), who was limited to begin Week 11. Bell's status could afford Kevin Coleman Jr. additional opportunities, although the low-volume Miami pass offense remains unlikely to support more than one pass catcher, now playing with a backup quarterback in Kyle McCord.

Maye is believed to have suffered a fractured ankle, an injury that would sideline him for the remainder of the 2026 season. Impact: As of Tuesday, the team continues to gather more information on the injury sustained in the first half of the Week 10 loss to the Lions. The team is also reportedly reaching out to quarterbacks as they look to right a sinking ship following consecutive losses for the first time in head coach Mike Vrabel's tenure. More to come on this developing story. Suffice to say, the fantasy value of the primary skill position players in New England takes a significant hit for the remainder of the year.

Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum.

Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined.

Brown missed Week 8 and Week 9 with ankle and knee issues before returning for Week 10 against the Lions, only to pick up a hamstring injury. The team is reportedly gathering more information during their Week 11 bye.

Impact: DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, Mack Hollins, and Kyle Williams led the team in snaps and routes in the absence of Brown in Week 9, with none of the bunch consistent fantasy producers. Fantasy managers are likely forced to wait until more information is released to gauge Brown's expected status in Week 12.

Henderson was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 10 and will miss the next four games, at minimum.

Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are likely to form a one-two punch in the absence of Henderson, with Stevenson the favorite to lead the team in opportunities and snaps. Stevenson can be viewed as a volume-backed RB2 for the time being.

Smith departed the team's Week 10 loss with an ankle injury. Follow-up testing confirmed the injury is not considered serious but his status for Week 11 against the Chiefs is in doubt. He was officially limited on Wednesday.

Impact: The fantasy upside of all primary skill position players for the Jets would take a significant hit should Smith be unavailable against the Chiefs. Fantasy managers will want to monitor this situation closely in the coming days.

Cooper aggravated the same ankle injury he has been dealing with for multiple weeks in Week 10, placing his status in doubt for Week 11. He was sidelined to begin the week.

Impact: Target volume would likely concentrate further on Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell should Cooper be unable to play against the Chiefs. Isaiah Williams (ribs) is also hurt.

Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers, who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings. Recent signee Jacoby Brissett is expected to start under center in Week 10.

Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills.

Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done.

Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role.

The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3. The team activated his 21-day practice window this week but he is listed as doubtful to play in Week 10 against the Steelers.

Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable.

All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: All loses yet another season in devastating fashion after suffering his third torn ACL. His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki, although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy.

Impact: He will be eligible to return after four games missed.

Pittman was limited on Wednesday before being seen using a scooter in the locker room after practice. It was then revealed that Pittman aggravated his foot injury. The Steelers placed him on injured reserve late in Week 5. Pittman was limited to begin Week 11 after the Steelers designated him to return.

Impact: Pittman's potential return could lower Germie Bernard's target share. Head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that the team is hopeful Pittman and Wilson can return for Week 11.

The Steelers designated Wilson to return from his Week 5 finger injury in Week 11. He is practicing fully.

Marks will not play in Week 11 after suffering a concussion in Week 10.

Impact: David Montgomery is tentatively expected to return from injury and should see the bulk of the opportunities out of the backfield, with Emari Demercado now on hand to operate in the primary change of pace role. Montgomery is a viable RB2, if active.

Harrison will miss another game after injuring his hamstring in practice in Week 10.

Impact: Hamstring injuries can be tricky for wide receivers. Kayshon Boutte and Xavier Hutchinson would mildly benefit with Harrison sidelined.

Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats.

Head coach DeMeco Ryans said in Week 5 that Montgomery is "week-to-week" with a groin injury. He is set to return for the Texans' Thursday Night Football game against the Colts.

Impact: Montgomery is a volume-backed RB2 if he returns for Week 11. Emari Demercado would fill those shoes should Montgomery miss.

The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7.

Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined.

Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp.

Impact: It's a massive blow to a Texans team that was counting on Higgins taking another step forward in his Sophomore campaign. The team traded for Kayshon Boutte in the wake of the injury and then added Marvin Harrison Jr. in a deal with the Cardinals ahead of Week 6.

Pierce aggravated the injury that required offseason surgery in Week 2. The Colts placed him on injured reserve in Week 3. He will attempt to avoid surgery by rehabbing his injured heel. Head coach Shane Steichen said he is unsure whether Pierce will play again this season.

Impact: Tyler Warren is the de facto top option through the air for the remainder of the season.

Impact: He is not fantasy-relevant in 12-team leagues, but losing him would further condense the pass-catching corps.

Tuten played in Week 9 without practicing. He played in Week 10 while practicing minimally, and he begins Week 11 limited.

Impact: His health is improving. Tuten is an RB1.

Rodriguez played through the injury in Week 9 and remained limited early in Week 10. He was removed from the injury report Friday and will play against the Titans. Rodriguez remains limited in practice, but will play.

Tate begins Week 11 limited, and is tentatively on track to return from his multi-week injury.

Impact: Tate would be in the WR2/3 range against the Cowboys, if active.

Robinson suffered an ankle injury in Week 10 and will be sidelined for the rest of the year.

Impact: Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike enter the matchup-based FLEX tier.

Spears has been nursing a knee injury for weeks and begins Week 11 limited.

Impact: Spears does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

Waddle suffered a concussion in the team's Week 9 win over the Panthers. He is practicing in full for Week 11.

Impact: Waddle returns to the volatile WR3 tier.

Harvey popped on the injury report Thursday with a knee injury and was ruled out for Week 8 on Friday. He was placed on injured reserve Saturday and will miss the next four weeks, at minimum.

Impact: Jonah Coleman is an RB2, operating as the team's starter.

Walker was added to the injury report for Week 10's Friday practice and was ultimately ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. He remains sidelined to begin Week 11.

Impact: Emmett Johnson is an RB1 for as long as Walker is sidelined. We expect Walker to be held out in Week 11.

Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks.

Impact: The team has lost all ability to attack downfield without Thornton, meaning our fantasy interest should be confined to those with expected volume.

Bowers picked up an ankle injury in the team's Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. He did not practice the following Wednesday.

Impact: Head coach Klint Kubiak relayed Monday that the injury is not considered serious, though he tends to downplay injuries. Michael Mayer is tentatively in line to start.

McConkey reportedly experienced back spasms during warmups for Week 9 and ultimately did not play. He did not play in Week 10. McConkey was limited to begin Week 11.

Impact: McConkey would be a WR3 if active.

Ferguson departed the team's Week 9 win with an ankle injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that the veteran tight end is "expected to miss time." He was ruled out for Week 10 and remains sidelined in Week 11.

Impact: Brevin Spann-Ford is on hand to handle primary tight end duties. He is not a recommended streaming option outside of the deepest leagues.

Davis was placed on injured reserve and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season.

Expect Israel Abanikanda to be elevated to the active roster from the practice squad for Week 2, while Williams appears likely to see all the work he can handle against the Commanders. Williams is a locked-in RB1.

The team sent Goodson to injured reserve Saturday.Impact: The Cowboys have struggled with depth in the backfield all season, which takes another blow in the absence of Goodson. Israel Abanikanda was signed to the active roster and will serve as the primary change of pace option behind Javonte Williams in the immediate future. Williams remains a locked-in RB2 with one of the more robust roles in the league.

Dart injured his MCL, PCL and meniscus on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football against the Rams. He will undergo surgery to address the MCL and meniscus and miss the rest of the regular season. Giants head coach John Harbaugh said it is possible for Dart to return in the postseason, although this is unlikely.

Impact: Backup Jameis Winston was benched in favor of recent acquisition J.J. McCarthy in the second half of their loss to the Saints. Head coach John Harbaugh confirmed McCarthy as the starter for Week 7.

Skattebo is practicing in full for Week 11.

Impact: None. He is a low-end RB1 with six teams on bye.

Pierce was injured on a kick return in the fourth quarter of the team's Week 7 loss to the Cowboys. He was placed on injured reserve the following Wednesday.

Smith has repeatedly aggravated the hamstring strain he initially injured in August. He was limited to begin Week 11 and told reporters he is 100 percent healthy.

Impact: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also limited. Both players are tentatively on track to play in Week 11, though only Smith needs to be in 12-team lineups.

Team doctors discovered a blood clot in Hurts' calf. He was ruled out for Week 6 and could be looking at an extended absence. He was placed on injured reserve on Saturday after more clots were found in his lungs.

Shipley reportedly suffered a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot in Week 5. He resumed practicing in a limited capacity in Week 11.

Barkley is no longer listed with a back injury and is practicing in full post-bye.

Impact: His health is improving. Barkley is an RB1.

McLaurin suffered a season-ending patellar tendon rupture in Week 6.

Impact: Stefon Diggs will likely serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver moving forward.

Lane suffered a dislocated ankle and fracture in Week 4 and is likely done for the season.

Impact: Minimal. Lane was primarily a special teams contributor.

Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice this week and ruled out for Week 6 against the 49ers. The team then placed him on injured reserve. He was designated to return from injured reserve Monday.

Impact: Croskey-Merritt should resume his lead-rushing role upon returning.

McNichols suffered a foot injury in Week 8 and was placed on injured reserve in Week 9.

Impact: Rachaad White and veteran Austin Ekeler are suddenly the only two healthy backs on the Washington roster, neither of whom is an overly exciting fantasy option on a struggling offense. White is the preferred option and could be started as a viable FLEX, should McNichols miss time.

Monangai is practicing in full for Week 11.

Kmet suffered a season-ending knee injury in the team's Thursday Night Football win over the Patriots.

Jacobs suffered a fractured finger in the team's Week 9 win over the Patriots. He will miss two-to-three weeks after undergoing surgery.

Reed suffered a scary-looking neck injury that required stabilization in the team's Week 2 win over the Jets. Hockenson missed Week 10, but was limited to begin Week 11.

#2698. Nvidia has lost $2 trillion in value. Here's what options traders expect from earnings

Jensen Huang's forced exit from Nvidia shocked Wall Street and Washington, wiped $2 trillion off its market value, and raised serious questions about national security and regulation of the AI complex. Traders, for the moment, must content themselves with the comparatively mundane business of Tuesday's earnings, and options traders are expecting big moves.

With volatility in the stock near the highest since April 2025, options traders are now pricing a 7% reaction in the stock after its report, the biggest implied move going into an Nvidia report since February 2025, and well above the median move of 3.2% over the last eight quarters.

Implied volatility reached 68 Monday, compared to under 40 in early October, according to ThinkOrSwim data. Nvidia vol reached a multi-year high above 92 in the aftermath of President Trump's tariff Liberation day in April '25. In other words, the company that for much of the AI boom was the most reliable winner in the market, is now more volatile than all but 35 companies in the S&P 500.

"Longer term, I see significant downside risk unless Nvidia can attract an exceptional leader, someone like Tim Cook or AMD's Lisa Su," Nigam Arora, founder of the Arora report, said in a text ahead of the company's after-market report on Tuesday.

Since hitting all-time highs in October, Nvidia shares have fallen 35%, shedding $2 trillion in market capitalization along the way. Including Nvidia, there are only five companies in the S&P 500 worth more than $2 trillion. However, there is evidence that bulls have been holding out hope while bears snatch up profits: the ratio of open puts to call contracts has actually widened towards calls, according to Barchart data. The ratio is currently 0.87, down from a one-year high of 1.02 two weeks ago and the lowest since the first week of October.

The most popular contract by volume on Monday was the 155-strike put expiring at the bell Monday, but the most popular trade for later expiry was the 160-strike call expiring Thursday, and the second-most-common purchase was the 190-strike call expiring Friday, SpotGamma data show.

One catch is that most call contracts traded Monday looked like neutral to bearish positions opened by traders selling calls. Of the 5 million options traded on Monday, 3 million were calls, but more were likely opened by sellers than buyers. Of the $2.3 billion in options premium traded on Nvidia Monday, $1.2 billion was tied to puts, SpotGamma data show.

With bears taking profits in puts the past month, there's another potential snag on open interest. There are very few open put contracts at or below the $157 level at which the stock closed Monday. That suggests any bad surprise would find many traders with little downside protection.

By the same token, there's notable open interest in call contracts from the 175-strike and above, suggesting profit-taking on a bounce could limit Nvidia's recovery past levels it breached over the past week.

Either way, Tuesday's earnings could provide fireworks.

#2696. Closer, but not enough for Rebels to avoid loss in Players Era 8

LAS VEGAS — Well, at least it was more competitive.Pretty, it wasn't.But whether you get blown out by 25 points or fall by 15, a loss is a loss. And for UNLV, it was another frustrating night at Michelob Ultra Arena in the Players Era 8 basketball event.Yes, the Runnin' Rebels weren't embarrassed by Auburn. But despite their own shortcomings the Tigers managed to do enough things right to win 86-71 and send Josh Pastner's team to its second straight loss after they started the season 3-0.UNLV will try to avoid being swept in the Players Era for a second consecutive year when it faces Rutgers at 5 p.m. Thursday at MUA. Last year, the Scarlet Knights defeated the Rebels 80-65.In the championship game, Houston, which knocked off No. 1 Florida 86-76, will face Kansas, which rallied to get by West Virginia 86-82 to set up an all-Big 12 title matchup."Our guys fought and competed," Pastner said. "But we don't usually see this kind of size in the Mountain West. It's a different situation in the Players Era."The Tigers, who are big up front, including 7-0, 280-pound Narcisse Ngoy, who was drafted by the Atlanta Hawks in the second round of last year's NBA Draft after playing professionally in France, gave UNLV trouble inside. Bukky Oboye, who is 7-1 and played at Santa Clara before transferring, really caused the foul-plagued Rebels problems, particularly in the second half as he went to town down low and would finish with 14 points.So while Kansas' speed did UNLV in Tuesday, Auburn's size was their undoing Wednesday. Even a lousy night at the free-throw line couldn't deter the Tigers. They were a miserable 7 of 16 from the stripe, including an 0-for-4 performance from Ngoy, which on most nights would ultimately lead to their undoing.Not this night, however. Not when their opponent shot the ball poorly from anywhere on the court.The Rebels were 39 percent from the floor and made just 5 of 17 3-point attempts. Somehow, they outrebounded Auburn 39-38.Still, it was another double-digit loss. And what has to hurt for UNLV was it was well within striking range in the second half, having pulled within three, 47-44, with plenty of time to come all the way back.Instead, Auburn went inside to Oboye, got some outside shooting from Adam Olsen to balance things out as the Vancouver-area native had five made 3-pointers and would finish with 15 points. It was a nice complement to guard Tahaad Pettiford, who despite foul trouble led Auburn with 22 points."We had a chance in the second half," Pastner said, referring to getting within three. "They finished with some lobs, we had a couple of misses, turnovers and they were able to extend it again. But credit to Auburn, their bigs did a good job."Tyrin Jones and Cam Miles led UNLV with 16 points apiece but it wasn't near enough. Sebastian Mack struggled, as the team's leading scorer managed to make just 3 of 12 shots and finished with nine points in 33 minutes.Miles said it's on him to make sure his team sustains its offense when it falls behind."As the point guard, I need to get my guys the ball in the right spots," he said. "I need to make the right plays."Perhaps. But missing open looks and bricking free throws along with surrendering layups and dunks will get you beat every time.So once again, UNLV will look to regroup in less than 24 hours, try and find its game over 40 minutes against a Rutgers team whose coach, Steve Pikiell, is battling cancer and is on a leave of absence from the program, and which took Notre Dame to overtime before falling 110-100 Wednesday."It's not a problem of competing," Pastner said. "We had chances (vs. Auburn). We just didn't capitalize on them."

#2695. 3 things that led to the Mavericks’ cathartic 116-94 blowout win over the Golden State Warriors

The Dallas Mavericks (8-7) handled business Wednesday night, beating the shorthanded Golden State Warriors (8-7) 116-94 in a game Dallas controlled almost from the start. Cooper Flagg led the way with 33 points, five rebounds, nine assists and three steals on 11-of-15 shooting, while P.J. Washington added 21 points and hit five threes. Kyrie Irving finished with 17 points, six rebounds, five assists and three steals, and Dallas shot 50.6 percent from the field and 41.5 percent from distance. Golden State never found much offense without Stephen Curry, Jimmy Butler and Kristaps Porzingis, and once Dallas pushed the lead to 20 by the end of the third quarter, the game was essentially over.

Dallas jumped all over Golden State in the first quarter, starting with Flagg and Irving controlling almost everything. The duo scored or assisted on 22 of the Mavericks' first 25 points, setting the tone for a 19-2 Dallas run that quickly created separation. Flagg was perfect in the quarter, scoring 10 points on 3-of-3 shooting, while Kyrie added six points and two assists. P.J. Washington also caught fire early, hitting all three of his 3-point attempts, and Dallas shot 57.1 percent from the field and 50 percent from deep. Golden State, meanwhile, looked lost offensively for long stretches and shot just 38.5 percent. The Warriors found a little life late, but Dallas still led 35-25 after one.

Golden State showed more resistance in the second quarter, but Dallas remained firmly in control. The Warriors forced a few sloppy turnovers and cut into the lead, but Flagg quickly settled things down. He scored 12 points in the quarter and reached 22 by halftime, attacking the rim, getting to the line, and knocking down another three while shooting 7-of-9 overall. Washington was just as important, finishing with 16 points, four threes, and another reliable source of offense for Dallas. The Mavericks shot 53.8 percent from the field, 45.5 percent from three, and went 10-for-10 at the line in the half, taking a 62-49 lead into the break.

Dallas blew the game open in the third quarter and turned a comfortable lead into a rout. The Warriors were shooting just 41.4 percent from the field and 25 percent from three through three quarters, with Brandin Podziemski struggling badly from deep. Dallas kept stacking stops, moving the ball and getting quality looks, and by the end of the quarter the Mavericks had pushed the lead to 20 at 92-72. At that point, the game was over.

The fourth quarter was basically a formality. Dallas had already put the game away in the third, so the final 12 minutes were mostly about getting through it healthy and letting the bench finish things off. Flagg stayed in just long enough to finish with 33 points, five rebounds and nine assists, and the Mavericks cruised to a 116-94 win. Golden State never seriously threatened again, and Dallas emptied the bench to close out a pretty uneventful final quarter.

Flagg had been in a rough stretch by his standards over the last few games, so this was about as emphatic of a response as Dallas could have asked for. Flagg was in control from the opening minutes and finished with 33 points, five rebounds, nine assists and three steals while shooting 11-of-15 from the field, 3-of-5 from three and 8-of-8 at the line. He was aggressive without forcing anything, got downhill whenever he wanted, and looked much more comfortable creating for everyone around him.

The nine assists were especially encouraging because they showed he wasn't just hunting his own shot to break out of the slump. He read the floor, made the right play, and controlled the game. After a few quieter performances, this looked much more like the version of Flagg Dallas has come to expect.

Washington needed this one too. His jumper had gone cold during the road trip, but he looked completely different against Golden State, knocking down five threes and finishing with 21 points on 7-of-10 shooting. He hit three threes in the first quarter alone and helped Dallas create separation before the Warriors could settle into the game. When Washington is making shots like this, the Mavericks become so much harder to defend because teams cannot load everything toward Flagg and Kyrie Irving. It was only one game, but seeing the ball go through the net again should be a nice confidence boost after the way he had been shooting.

There really is not much more complicated than this — Golden State doesn't have much if the Warriors don't have Curry in the lineup. The Warriors were without Curry, Butler and Porzingis, but Curry's absence was especially obvious because Golden State had almost no reliable way to generate offense. The Warriors shot 42.7 percent from the field and an ugly 23.7 percent from three, with Brandin Podziemski going 0-of-5 from deep and Yang Hansen Lendeborg finishing 6-of-18 from the field.

Dallas deserves credit for taking advantage, but there were long stretches where Golden State simply looked incapable of creating a good shot. Once the Mavericks pushed the lead out in the third quarter, nobody on the other side could drag the Warriors back into it. This was a shorthanded team that looked exactly like one.

#2694. NFL slams NBC's Mike Florio, Chris Simms for 'offensive' Mike Vrabel joke

The NFL is not happy with one of its primary media partners.

During a recent episode of "Pro Football Talk Live" on NBC Sports, Mike Florio and Chris Simms made a joke at the expense of New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel that included a thinly veiled reference to Adolf Hitler, although neither mentioned his name.

"He got the German mustache to go along with that right now, too," Simms said during a Nov. 17 edition of the show while discussing the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday in Munich, Germany. "So he was hitting all themes there over in Germany."

"You gotta be careful trimming that thing," Florio said. "Yeah, if you're in Germany, you gotta be careful trimming the sides of that thing."

Between a lot of laughs, Simms and Florio kept the bit going for a few more seconds, although an off-air producer must have appeared to wish the duo didn't go down that road.

"It was eighty years ago," Florio said. "Let us have some fun, for crying out loud."

The exchange did not sit well within NFL headquarters.

"We found the remarks inappropriate and offensive," the NFL said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports from executive vice president of communications, policy and public affairs Jeff Miller

Both Florio and Simms contribute to NBC's elbow coverage of "Sunday Night Football." Simms had previously been part of "Football Night in America" but was removed from the show this offseason. The duo apologized Thursday.

"On yesterday's (Nov. 17) PFT Live show, we made comments that some found offensive and we apologize," Simms and Florio said in a joint statement via NBC Sports.

#2693. Lions place Aidan Hutchinson on IR, activate Kerby Joseph

While one Lions player is out, another is on his way back in.

Detroit announced on Wednesday afternoon that the club has placed defensive end Aidan Hutchinson on injured reserve and activated safety Kerby Joseph off of the reserve/physically unable to perform list.

Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL during the Lions’ victory over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday. It’s the second season-ending injury in the last three years for Hutchinson, who missed most of 2024 with a fractured tibia and fibula.

Joseph has been sidelined by knee issues that limited him to six games last season. He was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. Head coach Dan Campbell has said that Joseph is expected to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday.

Additionally, the Lions have re-signed defensive back Nick Whiteside to the club’s practice squad.

#2692. Lakers Player Ratings: Doncic Has Inefficient Game As Winning Streak Gets Snapped By Jazz

The Los Angeles Lakers' nine-game winning streak ended with a frustrating 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz. Luka Doncic struggled to find his shooting rhythm, finishing with 29 points but needing 28 attempts to get there.

His nine turnovers were particularly costly, as Utah kept turning defensive pressure into fast-break opportunities.

The Lakers never found consistent offensive production outside of Doncic and Quentin Grimes, who finished with 20 points, seven rebounds, and four assists. Utah, meanwhile, received a balanced offensive performance led by Keyonte George's 30 points and 10 assists. Ace Bailey added 19 points, while Josh Green was perfect from the field, scoring 11 points on 4-4 shooting.

The difference was efficiency. Utah shot 48.1% from the field and 37.8% from three-point range, compared to just 38.2% and 27.3%, respectively, for Los Angeles. The Jazz also committed 21 turnovers, but the Lakers couldn't capitalize enough to overcome their shooting struggles.

Here are the Lakers' player ratings from the loss.

Game Stats: 20 PTS, 7 REB, 4 AST, 1 TOV, 8-20 FG, 4-10 3-PT FG, 35 MIN

Grimes was the Lakers' second-leading scorer and one of the few players who consistently provided offensive production. He knocked down four three-pointers and contributed seven rebounds and four assists. However, his 8-20 shooting wasn't particularly efficient, and he couldn't do enough to compensate for Doncic's struggles. Still, he was one of the more dependable Lakers on a difficult night.

Game Stats: 29 PTS, 5 REB, 7 AST, 2 STL, 9 TOV, 10-28 FG, 2-12 3-PT FG, 7-7 FT, 37 MIN

Doncic still managed to score 29 points, but this was a frustrating performance by his standards. He shot just 35.7% from the field and an especially poor 16.7% from three-point range. The nine turnovers were arguably even more damaging, repeatedly giving Utah opportunities to control the game. His seven assists and 7-7 free-throw shooting kept his offensive production respectable, but the inefficiency and ball security issues were too much to overlook.

Game Stats: 10 PTS, 11 REB, 1 AST, 1 TOV, 3-7 FG, 4-10 FT, 31 MIN

Kessler recorded a double-double, collecting 11 rebounds while scoring 10 points. His five offensive rebounds helped the Lakers generate second-chance opportunities, but his free-throw shooting was a major issue. Making just four of 10 attempts left too many points at the line, particularly in a game where Los Angeles struggled to score efficiently. The rebounding was valuable, but the missed free throws hurt.

Game Stats: 12 PTS, 1 AST, 3 TOV, 4-8 FG, 1-2 3-PT FG, 3-3 FT, 20 MIN

Sexton gave the Lakers a useful scoring contribution off the bench, finishing with 12 points on 50% shooting. He also converted all three free throws and knocked down a three-pointer. However, three turnovers and a lack of rebounding or defensive production kept this from being a stronger performance. The Lakers could have used more of his scoring in the second half.

#2690. Cam Skattebo done with backflip celebration in wake of Aidan Hutchinson injury

That's the message from New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo in regard to his famed touchdown celebration. Skattebo, who has never been one to shy away from contact or a moment to celebrate, saw all he needed to see when it came to Aidan Hutchinson's season-ending injury.

The Detroit Lions' star celebrated a sack of New England Patriots QB Drake Maye by jumping in the air. When Hutchinson landed, he suffered a torn ACL.

And that was enough for Skattebo to retire his backflip celebration – at least for the time being.

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters, via the New York Post's Ryan Dunleavy, after Wednesday's practice. "I'm saying yeah (no more). Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me."

This isn't the first time that the running back's celebration has been a topic of discussion.

Skattebo was seen on video backflipping multiple times last offseason, despite coming off a serious season-ending ankle injury in 2025. It got to a point where new head coach, John Harbaugh, was asked for his reaction. Harbaugh joked about the situation, saying in part, "Dude, at least stick it."

The 24-year-old brought the celebration back to the field in the Giants' season opener when he scored a touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys.

At the time, he left the door open for a new celebration to emerge, but the backflip resurfaced again as recently as Week 10 against the Washington Commanders on "Thursday Night Football."

So is the backflip done? Maybe for now. Or maybe not.

Skattebo noted it could come back in a big moment, like if the Giants make the playoffs.

In other words, Skattebo and the backflip are taking a break. History says they'll be back together soon enough though.

#2689. Cam Skattebo says he's done doing backflips after Aidan Hutchinson injury

Giants running back Cam Skattebo’s penchant for backflips became a talking point during his recovery from last season’s ankle injury, but he resumed doing them after touchdowns upon his return to action this fall.

Skattebo said that those days are now done, however. Skattebo said on Wednesday that he’s retiring the celebration in the wake of seeing Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL after a post-sack celebratory leap last Sunday.

“It’s hard to see,” Skattebo said, via Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post. “I’m saying yeah [no more]. Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.”

Skattebo did reserve the right to bring the celebration out of retirement “if we go to the playoffs or something,” but it seems any touchdowns in the immediate future will be marked with a more reserved reaction.

#2688. Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 11

The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position are available.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. TB) - 127.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs is the 1.01 in fantasy points over replacement per game (+15.9) and only trails Jaxon Smith-Njigba in winning percentage on Yahoo. Seems good.

Tampa Bay has been stout against the position, ranking 32nd in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields and holding recent primary rushers like Bijan Robinson (RB28), D'Andre Swift (RB50), Chuba Hubbard (RB34) and Jaylen Warren (RB23) in check. Detroit heads into the home matchup with an implied total of 25.25 points (ninth) as 7-point home favorites. It's a difficult spot, but it's getting nearly impossible to not have him as the RB1 overall every week.

The Chiefs seem to be planning for Kenneth Walker III (groin) to rest another week after Johnson more than held his own in last week's blowout win. The rookie, who reminds me of a Bucky Irving type on film, handled 22 carries and six receptions, leading to 32.1 half PPR points on 20.6 expected points. Those are obviously elite RB1 numbers. Kansas City simply doesn't have another RB it trusts for the moment, and the offense is firing on all cylinders against mediocre opponents.

The Cardinals are just that. They've allowed the fifth-most rush YPG (130) and were just schooled by Blake Corum (119 total yards) last week. A huge 28.0-point team total as 15.5-point favorites (!!!!!!) awaits.

3. James Cook III (vs. MIA) - 110.5 proj. total yards

Cook ranks as the RB6 in half PPR points per game on RB8 usage across his last four contests, averaging 23 carries (second) and 109.8 rushing yards per game. He has scored a rushing touchdown in each of his last four games (what's new?), including a season-high 157 rushing yards on 18 carries in Week 10.

The Bills are expected to beat the Dolphins by 16.5 points with a bonkers 31-point team total. Miami just lost DTs Jordan Phillips and Zeek Biggers to injured reserve. I don't have to tell you this is a great spot.

4. Christian McCaffrey (vs. MIN) - 87.5 proj. total yards

When McCaffrey is in the United States of America this year, he averages 22.7 half PPR points (RB2) on 16.3 expected half PPR points (RB6). Turns out, Kaelon Black is a fine role player but nothing more than that to CMC. Remember to go outside in early September while the weather is nice.

Anyways, this will be a great test for the 49ers as they face the Vikings in Mexico City. They've been run on at times and won't have LB Blake Cashman, but that's about as negative as I can get on what otherwise is an elite defense. They've been fifth best against fantasy RBs this year (16.7 half PPR per game), though fantasy RB1s have held the line; James Cook III (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8). We can ding CMC's projection with the Niners projected for 24.25 points versus their current 31.75 points per game, but it can only go so far. He's a mid-range RB1.

5. Chuba Hubbard (vs. BAL) - 109.5 proj. total yards

The Ravens defense has been one of the more underwhelming units. Their secondary has been better than their run defense, to the point that even Omarion Hampton ran well up the gut against them last Monday night. It's a shorter week for Baltimore, who is now trending out of the playoff picture. We'll see how much fight it has left. The Panthers have a 23.0-point team total (12th) as near-field-goal favorites.

6. Javonte Williams (vs. TEN) - 94.5 proj. total yards

Let's keep this simple: Williams is an upside RB1 whenever the Cowboys have a 31.5-point team total, as they do here.

The Titans have allowed nearly 1,500 yards over their last three games, the most in a 3-game stretch in their franchise history. Trading away mega-star DT Jeffery Simmons and Pro Bowl-caliber S Amani Hooker won't help. The starting RB against Tennessee has cleared 100 total yards in four straight contests.

7. Bucky Irving (at DET) - 85.5 proj. total yards

This assumes Jalon Daniels is back at QB with Baker Mayfield (foot) picking up a new injury during the bye week. The Bucs are likely going to be extremely run-heavy, as they've been for the past two months with the OL smoking defenses up front. Irving has been the RB7 on RB11 usage this season, with 21.0+ half PPR points in 4 of 5 recent games. He's averaged 22.2 carries during that stretch, with games against pretty easy opponents. That's too big to fail, especially given how slippery he is on tape.

The Lions are a pass funnel typically, but the losses of LB Jack Campbell, EDGE Aidan Hutchinson and CB D.J. Reed (questionable) make them fairly bad in both phases. They still have some DTs to worry about, but the Bucs should be able to run it here, despite the spreadsheets suggesting otherwise. Tampa Bay will attempt to bleed out the clock as 7-point road dogs with a team total of 18.25 points (21st). Irving should absorb a lot of that team total.

8. Derrick Henry (at CAR) - 78.5 proj. total yards

The Ravens are going to pass more with Jacoby Brissett at QB and with the OL struggling, especially when first-round rookie LG Vega Ioane isn't on the field. Henry can still score goal-line touchdowns as he did on Monday night, but a real reset is warranted in terms of efficiency and rushing volume if the Ravens aren't expected to be crushing teams as often as they would've with Lamar Jackson, who is hoping to return around Week 16 if things go to plan. In the meantime, it's possible Henry catches an extra target or two based on the scheme changing, but that won't even out the loss of projected touchdowns. He'll settle in as a boom-bust RB2 the rest of the way.

The Panthers have cleaned things up with better health and a new DC recently, but Carolina has bled fantasy points to RBs (24.8, third) across the season. It was Jonah Coleman (RB6) two weeks ago and Josh Jacobs (RB11) and Bucky Irving (RB2) before that. A 21.0-point team total isn't the worst thing this week, with six teams on bye and five others projected for fewer than 17.0.

9. Jonah Coleman (vs. LV) - 99.5 proj. total yards

With R.J. Harvey (knee) on IR, the backfield has been down to just two. Coleman leapfrogged J.K. Dobbins over the last pair of games, finishing as the RB7 and RB9 in expected half PPR points. Dobbins won't play on passing downs, so Coleman is grabbing some receptions alongside his rushing role. He has been just fine on tape in a good situation.

Speaking of, the Raiders are generous when it comes to fantasy points for RBs. They've allowed, oh, just 176 rushing yards per game this month. Both Seahawks RBs played well behind three backup linemen, and CMC (RB4), Braelon Allen (RB7) and Kyren Williams (RB12) were fantasy RBs this month. Denver is listed as 10-point home favorites with an implied team total of 25.25 points (eighth).

10. Tony Pollard (at DAL) - 85.5 proj. total yards

Pollard has been the RB8, RB3 and RB1 most recently, and it's simply been because he's breaking a ton of tackles. It's hard to believe it'll be sustainable, as star LG Peter Skoronski is on injured reserve, but Pollard is also the RB10 in expected points this month, with Cam Ward taking his game up a tier. It's still a painful offense on the whole and the floor can fall out at any point. It's best to stay tethered to his RB15 on RB16 usage standing across the entire year sample. Hopefully Carnell Tate (shoulder) can return to make the offense more potent.

The Cowboys are pathetic on defense. They've removed their sitting DC from play-calling duties, while their starters have missed a ton of tackles in crucial spots. They also don't play sound against the run, which is why they've allowed the most fantasy points to RBs (27.0) and most rushing yards per game (154) this season. Last week's 44.3 eruption from Christian McCaffrey against them was the best fantasy outing of the year by any player at any position. Beyond that, opponents facing Dallas have passed at a 47% rate in neutral situations, which is the third-lowest neutral pass rate allowed in the league. Tennessee enters as 8.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 23 points (13th).

11. Chase Brown (at WAS) - 74.5 proj. total yards

The Bengals have largely abandoned the run, which arguably isn't even a bad thing for Brown. Cincy is up to 30.9 points per game because it's first in passing success rate. Brown has a better chance of lucking into touchdowns if the team passes its way down to the goal line. We saw that happen last week when each of his scores came through the air, both out of structure.

Aside from the scores, Brown tallied eight receptions as a check-down option with space to operate, as defenses are going to have to play softer and softer coverage against these alien WRs. Brown can be forgettable as a talent on a severely pass-heavy offense, and still finish as a low-end RB1 in fantasy due to the scoring bonanza. He's the RB1 in receptions per game (5.2).

The next victim of the Bengals' offense will be the Commanders, who don't have two of their top DTs and were struggling through the air before anyway. The Bengals are up to a 30.5-point team total.

12. D'Andre Swift (vs. NO) - 83.5 proj. total yards

Kyle Monangai (toe) is back. Here are Swift's splits with him since Week 5 of last year, when the offense became the version we have today.

For context, 13.9 half PPR points is the RB16 right now, while 13.0 expected points is the RB17. Those are probably closer to his per-game floor the rest of the way, but it is a real reset for Swift's baseline projection. He can still have RB1 moments with Monangai. They will just happen less often.

The Saints are a great spot to sneak in a fantasy RB1 moment! They've allowed the second-most fantasy points to RBs on the sixth-most rushing yards per game (130). Chuba Hubbard ran right through tackles last week, something that's happened way too often this year. Chicago has a monster 30.0-point team total, so both backs are obvious starts.

13. Jaylen Warren (at PHI) - 95.5 proj. total yards

Warren has settled in as an upside RB2 with Rico Dowdle back in the mix. He's averaged 14.0 carries and 2.8 receptions this month, leading to RB17 on RB19 usage. The Steelers haven't played great ball on offense over that stretch and just watched LG Mason McCormick dislocate his ankle last week. The OL being great this season has certainly helped Warren, who has been a top-5 RB to my eyes this year beyond that.

The matchup is reassuring. This is an eruption spot, looking at the EPA numbers on the ground. The Eagles have struggled all year, then traded away run-stuffing DT Jordan Davis at the deadline. There are fewer reasons to be afraid of what used to be an impossible opponent, and the lines reflect that. Pittsburgh enters as 4.5-point road favorites with an implied team total of 21.5 points (15th).

14. Bhayshul Tuten (at NYG) - 92.5 proj. total yards

Tuten set a career high with 28.1 expected half PPR points last week, with 26 carries and three receptions. Many of those were failed goal-line attempts, but Tuten did score late en route to an RB10 on RB1 usage outing. He's now the RB10 on RB17 usage this season as a low-end RB1 with weekly upside. Chris Rodriguez Jr. will vulture the occasional touchdown, but otherwise, it's all Tuten now. The only marginal issue is that the already suspect Jaguars OL is now missing C Robert Hainsey (knee) for the next couple of weeks.

The Giants rank 25th in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs at 17.1 points per game. That includes ranking 23rd in points allowed on RB rushing plays (11.3 per game) and 20th on RB receiving plays (5.8 per game). Opposing lead rushers have routinely been held in check against them recently, with no RB clearly the top-24 over their past three games. DROY favorite Arvell Reese has a lot to do with that. Jacksonville heads on the road as 6-point favorites with an implied team total of 26.25 points (seventh). It's more of a mediocre matchup for Tuten.

15. David Montgomery (vs. IND) - 67.5 proj. total yards

Montgomery got in a full practice last Friday before being ruled out, but has practiced in full leading up to Thursday Night Football this week. Woody Marks (concussion) won't play, leaving Monty with Emari Demercado, who missed some lanes in the second half of last game. It won't be a surprise if the desperate Texans use Montgomery as a bell cow despite him being out since Week 5. They don't have a real choice. Of course, the Texans' bell cow RB hasn't been very valuable so far. Since Week 6, the Texans RBs are averaging 16.8 expected half PPR points per game with very mid efficiency. Montgomery finishing with 15-20 expected points shouldn't come as a surprise this week, considering the opponent.

The Colts haven't been competitive all year, especially without their best linemen on both sides of the ball. This month, Indy has allowed the sixth-most rushing yards per game (144). This season, they've allowed the sixth-most points to fantasy RBs (23.0). There really are no excuses for Houston this time around. They own a 28.5-point team total at home as 12.5-point favorites.

16. Omarion Hampton (vs. NYJ) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Hampton set season highs in fantasy points (17.0 half PPR) and usage (15.9 expected) last week, in their first win of the year. Hampton handled 22 carries in a run-heavy game plan that continued because the scoreboard finally allowed for it. The Chargers are first in neutral run rate (61%), so don't be surprised if Hampton's fantasy performances tick up if they can stay more competitive after a brutal schedule. You can see the extra carries in the second half of last week here:

On tape, Hampton was used slightly differently last week. He handled nine pitches, which is the second-most by a player in a single game all year. Instead of being pointed to the perimeter, many of them got him going straight downhill, where his attributes are maximized. They also ran more man concepts instead of the wide zone stuff OC Mike McDaniel typically calls for. It's a meeting in the middle between player and coach, one that was long overdue.

This week, the Chargers are favored. I repeat, the Chargers are favored against the Jets. They don't have their best run-stopping DT right now either, which has helped opposing teams rack up 154 rushing yards per game this month (fourth). James Cook III (RB7) and Kenneth Walker III (RB1) just went nuclear against them, but even Ollie Gordon II had 103 total yards and a score in Week 7, too. This is easily the best it's looked for Hampton since the games started this year.

17. Saquon Barkley (vs. PIT) - 75.5 proj. total yards

Barkley is impossible to get a grasp on due to his injuries, the moving parts on the OL and now Joe Milton at QB. In a part-time role on a lousy offense in three games before the bye, Barkley was the RB25, RB21 and RB20 on RB26 usage. He looked good when he was on the field, and the OL did seem to be in a bit of a better spot on tape. I can see him out-kicking those marks after the bye, which hopefully has allowed him to get healthier. The Eagles' offense is in a spot where they can fully clunker at any time, so the floor doesn't exist.

The matchup will be a challenge, of course. Milton versus the Steelers' pressure will put the team in bad spots. Pittsburgh is only allowing 83 rushing yards per game (30th), as teams have essentially stopped trying to run on them in neutral situations (61% pass, first). Philly can't afford to do that, so it'll be running into brick walls for Barkley, with the hopes he springs a few of them for explosives. A 17.0-point team total works against those odds. Barkley is a volume-based RB2 in the most optimistic of projections.

18. Cam Skattebo (vs. JAX) - 70.5 proj. total yards

Skattebo is back to bell-cow work with Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR and Najee Harris released. Devin Singletary failed in that role when Skattebo missed in Week 9, then Skattebo delivered an RB5 on RB6 usage outing in Week 10 against the Commanders. They've had extended rest to get Skattebo prepared for another heavy workload in a balanced offense. It won't be surprising to see Skattebo emerge as a fantasy RB2 for the rest of the way, especially if his three grabs from Week 10 hold up.

The Jaguars defense has been stingy to opposing backfields, ranking 29th in half PPR points allowed to RBs. They did concede an RB8 weekly finish to Tony Pollard in Week 10 without DT Jordan Davis and safety Jessie Bates active, though Jonathan Taylor managed just 4.7 points (RB37) against them in Week 8 when they did have a star run-stuffing DT. Opposing offenses have leaned heavily into the pass against Jacksonville with a 59% neutral pass rate (second highest). I doubt the Giants will do that too much given their coaches and personnel, but it's a difficult matchup regardless. New York enters as 6-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (18th).

19. Breece Hall (at LAC) - 70.5 proj. total yards

Hall has been the RB16 and RB21 in usage since returning from a quad injury. He's easily paced Braelon Allen in touches and played more receiving snaps last week after being eased in the game prior. Hall will stick in the 14-18 touch range most outings, while splitting the goal line role with the more downhill Allen. That'll put a cap on Hall's projections each week, but as long as Geno Smith is healthy, the OL is in good enough shape for them to remain balanced on offense. Hall is a fine RB2, while Allen is a shakier FLEX, even during the byes.

The Chargers represent an above-average matchup overall (duh), ranking 11th in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs at 21.1 per game. Los Angeles is sixth in points allowed on the ground, though they rank 27th against backs via the air. They're still without Derwin James. New York travels out west as 3.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 19.0 points (19th).

20. Kyle Monangai (vs. NO) - 55.5 proj. total yards

In 18 games with D'Andre Swift since Week 5 of last year, when the Bears offense ascended to the spot they are today, Monangai has averaged 9.9 half PPR points on 10.0 expected points. That's closer to his lower-end outcome at this point, and the Bears seem antsy to get Monangai back so they can begin spelling Swift after a stretch of too much volume. In four games this year, he's the RB16 (14.2) on RB21 usage (12.6 expected).

Fresh off the bye, the Bears should be at the peak of their powers. A date with a Saints team that can't tackle awaits. Chicago projects for 30.0 points. Monangai is an upside FLEX, possibly a straight-up RB2 given the constraints of the week.

21. Ollie Gordon II (at BUF) - 74.5 proj. total yards

Gordon is now playing with fire after ripping off explosives as a new starter back in September. He's down to RB25 on RB13 usage this past month, thanks to 20 carries and just 1.5 receptions per game. His efficiency could crater without Malik Willis, as it did last week when he was the RB18 on RB10 usage. Trickier defenses than the Colts will give Kyle McCord more trouble.

The Bills are waking up on defense with a new DC. They've seen multiple true breakouts from their DL, and they're more shored up at S with Amani Hooker in the mix and moving Cole Bishop more into the box where he's at his best. Even while going through some pains, the Bills are still only allowing 93.6 rushing yards per game (25th). It's a bad matchup for Ollie with a team total of just 14.5 points.

22. Jonathan Taylor (at HOU) - 76.5 proj. total yards

Taylor is no longer a fantasy RB1. Over the past month, with Seth McGowan earning more change-of-pace work, Taylor has dropped to RB16 in usage at 12.9 expected half PPR points per game. This matches the historical splits I mentioned last week based on how many points the Colts finish with. When Indy is held to under 21 points, Taylor is largely a fantasy RB2. Last week, McGowan converted a goal-line score on a drive Taylor was playing on. Taylor was stuffed on another drive's goal-line attempt, but it's no longer true bell-cow usage for Taylor.

Beyond that, the Colts ruled out both of their starting OTs and obviously traded away star LG Quenton Nelson the weeks prior. Having all of this backup talent on a short week against the Texans' DL is beyond concerning. The Colts have a 16.0-point team total as 12.5-point dogs. With a real receiving corps and a healthy OL in Week 3, Taylor was held to 68 scoreless yards against Houston. He also had 39 scoreless yards against them in Week 18 with a backup QB.

Coming off a Week 10 bye, the 2-7 Eagles will face the Steelers on Sunday.

#2680. Norris confident F1 not putting people at risk with Middle East races

Lando Norris is confident Formula One bosses are not putting the sport's 2,000-strong travelling circus at risk by ending the season in the Middle East.

Following Saturday's race on the Las Vegas Strip, the grid's 11 teams - 10 of which have bases in the UK - will head to Qatar for the penultimate round on November 29 before a concluding fixture in Abu Dhabi the following weekend.

Imola had been placed on standby to host the final race amid the ongoing United States-Iran conflict.

However, F1 chiefs confirmed last week that they will push ahead with completing the 23-round season, as planned, in the Middle East.

UK's current Foreign Office advice says the situation in the region "remains deeply unpredictable and the risk of escalation is high."

It adds that "British nationals in, or planning to travel through, the Middle East should be prepared for possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions," as well as "a risk of further attacks across the region at short notice."

But speaking in Las Vegas, 27-year-old Norris, who won the previous race in Sao Paulo, said: "I am looking forward to going. From my side, I am fine. It is a big team that we travel with, and it is more, 'what do they think?'

"But I have my friend's wedding in Bahrain next week, so I was planning on going there anyway, and then going on to Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

"So, from my side, it is not a concern. I just don't believe that this sport would put us at risk."

The rounds in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were cancelled earlier this year, although a 'Bahrain Grand Prix' was relocated to Malaysia's Sepang venue last month. Next year's calendar is due to begin in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

"I don't have any hesitation to go or know of anyone that is concerned," said Mercedes driver George Russell ahead of the concluding two rounds.

"I am sure some people have their reservations. But I know people who live in the region, and they have said it quite bluntly, that if they didn't feel comfortable, they wouldn't remain there with their families.

"There are a lot of terrible things going on in every region of the world, and you have got to trust in the people that say it is safe. F1 are not stupid, so there is zero concern from my side. Fingers crossed it'll all be fine."

Kimi Antonelli was crowned world champion last month in Mexico, while his Mercedes team wrapped up the constructors' title the following weekend in Sao Paulo. Red Bull's Max Verstappen leads the battle to finish as runner-up in the drivers' standings. The four-time world champion is 17 points clear of Russell and 18 ahead of Lewis Hamilton ahead of Saturday's night race.

Not by Chicago. But by their own lack of fight. Of fortitude.

Patrick Williams shoots over Danny Wolf during the first half of the Nets' 137-107 blowout loss to the Bulls on Nov. 18, 2026, at Barclays Center. Corey Sipkin for the NY POST

#2675. Charles Leclerc reveals the gadget he’s been "hiding" in his Ferrari

Charles Leclerc has revealed that he has already been wearing a WHOOP fitness tracker while driving his Ferrari, and says he has "nothing to hide" as Formula 1 prepares to put drivers' heart rates on screen.

F1 announced on Wednesday that WHOOP will become an official partner of F1, with drivers wearing its wristbands in the car. Data such as heart rate will be used in social media graphics and could even appear as live TV overlays as early as 2027.

F1 has not said how many drivers will take part, but Ferrari already stared its own partnership with WHOOP earlier this year, and Leclerc, Lewis Hamilton and the wider team already use the devices.

Asked in Las Vegas ahead of this weekend's race how he felt about his data being shown to the public, Leclerc said he had no objections.

"I don't have anything to hide in particular. Obviously I'm now an ambassador for WHOOP and I've been using the device for quite a long time now to track my recovery, my sleep, but also when I'm in the car," Leclerc said.

"And now there's an actual device that is certified by FIA that we can, without hiding it anymore, wear it while I'm driving. So it's a good thing. At least for me it's very useful."

Asked directly whether he had been wearing it in the car, Leclerc confirmed: "Yes."

The Monegasque said the question of how much data is shown on the broadcast still had to be decided.

"To show it to everybody is another matter that we'll for sure discuss, but I personally don't have any problems with it," he said.

The trackers measure heart rate and heart rate variability, as well as sleep and VO2 max among other data. F1 hopes this will help fans understand how physically demanding the cars are to drive.

"For decades, fans have had incredible insight into the cars, but less insight into the impact that races have on the drivers," said WHOOP chief executive Will Ahmed in the announcement.

Leclerc is fifth in the drivers' standings, and is still looking for a second win of the season after his victory at Silverstone in July.

The Las Vegas Grand Prix takes place on Saturday night, local time.

Jepchirchir won women's marathon gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and the world title last year. The 33-year-old Kenyan runner is also a former world record holder in the half marathon.

The AIU, which investigates doping in track and field on behalf of the sport's governing body World Athletics, issued a statement saying Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules.

She returned an adverse analytical finding for EPO from an out-of-competition sample collected in Kenya prior to her Sydney Marathon victory in late August.

#2665. 'Power Slap world title would change my life'

The next 24 hours could change Darren Godfrey's life.

The 38-year-old is aiming for Power Slap glory by becoming middleweight world champion in Doha, Qatar.

Godfrey, of Church Stretton, Shropshire, will face Isaiah Quinones, from California, who is reigning middleweight world champion, and boasts the most knockouts in Power Slap middleweight history.

"I know I've got a job to do, and he's the man that's stood in my way, I'll show him no mercy on the night but I'll shake his hand when I pick him up," Godfrey, known in the sport as Tarantula, told the BBC.

Power slapping is a popular but controversial sport involving competitors slapping each other as hard as they can across the face, and saw medics in 2024 warn that it could cause serious brain damage.

He said he believed he would be a world champion from the beginning of his career.

"The first time I ever slapped someone, I sent them right across the stage - so from that moment on, I knew I'd got some crazy power in this game," he continued.

He said a win would change everything - but not just for him.

"The life that the champions are living is totally different to the life that I'm living - I want that life for me and my family," he said.

"The sponsors and endorsements that some of these guys are getting is absolutely crazy, it's changing their lives.

"The night that I win that belt, I'm going to push the wife out of the bed and the belt is going to take her place."

Godfrey's tattoo, on his slapping hand, is a play on words relating to his surname [BBC]

Godfrey started out kickboxing, boxing and bare knuckle fighting, but was scouted to change career by the assistant to Ultimate Fighting Championship boss and promoter Dana White, who leads the Power Slap.

"They must've just thought I was a crazy dude with an iron chin," he said.

"I absolutely love it, compared to the bare knuckle where I was taking a lot of damage, broken bones.

"Power slaps is a good way for me to be able to put out there my power, without the risk of getting my face cut open and losing my teeth.

"I'm confident in my chin and I've learnt a lot of tricks over the years to generate more than most."

Unlike boxing, no head gear is allowed and defenders cannot duck to avoid blows. Even flinching is banned.

Opponents are scored based on the amount of damage they inflict and how well they cope with getting slapped themselves.

Looking ahead to the fight on Thursday, Godfrey said there was "no crowd like a power slap crowd".

"As soon as I see that man hit the canvas, as soon as I know I've connected, I know he's gone, some kind of feeling comes over you.

"If this is where my career ends, that's good enough for me, that's a career well spent for me."

In 2024, the medical experts screened videos of tournaments and wrote a warning letter in a leading journal, JAMA Surgery, about their findings.

#2664. Cavs react to Sam Merrill’s tough missed free throws: ‘We all trust him’

CLEVELAND — There's no tougher way to lose a basketball game than at the free-throw line. It's even worse when the culprit is arguably the best shooter on your team.

For Sam Merrill and the Cleveland Cavaliers, tonight was one of those losses.

Merrill came up empty on a pair of free throws with the Cavs trailing by one point to the Memphis Grizzlies and under 5 seconds to play. That isn't what you expect from a career 89% free-throw shooter.

Even so, the Cavs aren't upset with their sharpshooter.

"I mean, there's a reason I made the pass [to Merrill]," said Donovan Mitchell. "We all trust him, you know, and I would do it again tomorrow; I'd do it again the next night; you're not defined by two free throws at the end of the game."

Sometimes you make the right play and things don't work out. Mitchell was doubled by Memphis in the final seconds; that's why Merrill had the ball and was crashing towards the rim with a trailing defender. It was the correct approach from everyone — the final shots just didn't go in.

"I love the process; I love that he drove, he's so smart to drive the ball, that's what I look at," said Kenny Atkinson. "This is the sport, right? It happens to the best, but I loved how he got to the line."

None of that makes the loss feel any better. But, for what it's worth, the Cavs feel comfortable with the opportunity they had in front of them. It seems like they'll win that scenario more often than not.

It's also true that Cleveland had other avenues towards winning tonight's game. They couldn't get key stops in the fourth quarter, and Merrill wasn't the only player who missed a shot.

"I told him we're not in that situation if I knock down the corner three or if I hit the floater that I missed," said Mitchell. "So we can all point to something."

The beauty of basketball is another opportunity is almost always right around the corner. The Cavs have a fast turnaround with another home game against the Indiana Pacers on Friday.

"For [Merrill], go get 30 in a half against Indiana, and we'll be fine," Mitchell joked.

#2660. The real reason John Harbaugh opted to receive after Giants won coin toss

John Harbaugh was prepared for a curveball just minutes before kickoff.

The Giants — like most NFL teams — typically defer their choice to the second half if they win the opening coin toss. But they broke from the norm last game by choosing to receive.

Because of some strategic advantage specific to the Commanders?

No, because cornerback Tae Banks wouldn't have been ready if the Giants started the game on defense, backup Colton Hood was already banged up (dislocated finger) and backup Paulson Adebo was a healthy scratch.

It shows the level of thought and quick-thinking adjustments needed to be an NFL head coach.

"We had a little issue come up right before, in warmups, where … actually Tae got dinged on his shoulder, and he was getting looked at," Harbaugh said.

"So we weren't going to have him for the first series. So that being the case, we figured hopefully he'll be out here for the second series."

Gregory Desrosiers returned the opening kickoff 24 yards, and the offense picked up two first downs before punting.

"Offense was gracious enough to at least put some plays out there and buy some time," Harbaugh said, "and [Banks] was able to play. So that determined that decision."

Giants head coach John Harbaugh speaks at a press conference in East Rutherford, N.J., on Nov. 18, 2026. Robert Sabo for NY Post

CB Nic Jones (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.

OLB Malik Harrison (groin) and S Jason Pinnock (hip) were limited participants.

Returner Charlie Jones and CB Nikko Reed, who were cut Monday, returned to the practice squad. OL Geno VanDeMark and RB Eric Gray were released.

Struggling kicker Dominic Zvada, who has missed six field goals this season, was in on the Giants' off day Monday to work on his technique issue from the right hash mark.

"That's probably the thing you can work on the most for that position. Probably more than any other position," Harbaugh said.

"He had a great day [Wednesday]. He was dead on. He hit the middle pole — the camera pole — numerous times on it on kicking field goals. And from that amazing, scary right hash. Just nailed it."

#2659. Syracuse’s Garwey Dual Announces Presence With 4th College

NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 15: Garwey Dual #3 of the Syracuse Orange celebrates with Ryan Moesch #0 during the first half against the St. John's Red Storm at Madison Square Garden on November 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)

Garwey Dual has spent his college basketball career looking for a home.

The lanky guard may have finally found one at Syracuse University with the Orange.

Dual had played four solid games to begin the season, but it was on Wednesday night at home against the pesky Cornell Big Red that Dual was needed at a high level for the first time.

And when his number was called on this night, Dual delivered over and over.

He scored a career-high college points total, coming at his fourth different school in four years.

Dual was also efficient and involved his teammates while being a menace defensively.

Without Dual, Syracuse probably gets upset by Cornell. With him, they improved to 3-2 on the season.

GettyNEW YORK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 15: Garwey Dual #3 of the Syracuse Orange celebrates with Ryan Moesch #0 during the first half against the St. John's Red Storm at Madison Square Garden on November 15, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images)

Dual was the best player on the floor for most of Syracuse's win over Cornell.

He finished with 20 points on a ridiculous 8-for-9 from the floor, including 2-for-2 from 3-point range, as well as 2-for-2 from the foul line.

Dual added eight assists, four rebounds, three steals and a block. He turned the ball over twice.

He also swished a difficult, quick-release 3-pointer late in the game after a bad possession to rescue the Orange from disaster as Cornell was getting closer.

On a night when Ryan Moesch struggled to make an impact, and in which Kiyan Anthony didn't play in the second half, new SU head coach Gerry McNamara needed Dual to deliver, and he did.

Dual is playing with his fourth school in four years.

He began his collegiate journey at Providence in 2023-24, and he got one start.

Dual became a more regular starter in 2024-25 at Seton Hall, but the Pirates had a rough season.

For 2025-26, Dual joined McNeese, and they won the Southland Conference Tournament to make the NCAA Tournament.

With McNeese, Dual was fifth in the Southland Conference in assists per game (4.3) and totaled 56 steals for the season, third in the conference. When McNeese took on No. 1 Michigan during the year, Dual had 15 points and five rebounds.

Dual transferred once more for this season, and McNamara — who has said he followed Dual dating back to high school — brought him aboard.

Ironically, Dual is the classic guard type that would've been great at the top of Jim Boeheim's 2-3 zone. On Wednesday night, though, Boeheim was doing color commentary and praising Dual for his man-to-man defense in McNamara's system.

There will be bigger games ahead, but Dual showed SU can rely on him.
